definition_zh: 优点；长处；价值；功绩；值得
definition_en: a good quality that deserves praise; the real worth of something; a record of service that earns reward; and as a verb, to deserve something
core_image: 桌上摊着一份朴素的工作记录，密密麻麻的小字压过了封面上那个显赫的姓氏
scene: 评审室里只摆着几份匿名材料，桌上没有名片，也没有介绍人，评委们一页页翻过去，在纸边写下批注。 The panel chose the plainest proposal on merit alone.
sceneCN: 这里是「优点、真才实学」（第 1 个义项：值得称赞的长处）；句意为评审只凭方案自身的优点，选中了最朴素的那一份。图中可辨识物件：匿名材料、批注笔迹、空着的名片位。

derivatives.zh: 由 merit 加 -orious 构成，义为「值得称赞的；有功绩的」
由 merit 与 -cracy（统治）复合而成，义为「精英治理；唯才是举的制度」
由 de-（减损）加 merit 构成，义为「缺点；过失」
由 merit 加 -ed 构成，义为「应得的；理所应当的」

senses.title: A good quality that deserves praise
senses.definition: a quality or feature of a person or thing that is good and deserves to be praised
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物身上值得称赞的好品质、好特点
senses.example: The plan's main merit is that it costs almost nothing to run.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案最大的优点几乎不花钱就能运转。
senses.why: Latin meritum named what a person had earned, so the first sense of the word is the good thing in someone that makes praise seem earned rather than given.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 meritum 指一个人挣得、应得的东西，所以这个词的第一层含义就是人身上那处让人不得不称赞的好处——称赞像是被挣来的，而不是白送的。

senses.title: The real worth of something
senses.definition: the actual worth or value of something, weighed when people judge whether it is any good
senses.definitionCN: 事物本身的实际价值，是人们在判断好坏时所称量的东西
senses.example: The judges compared the merits of the two designs before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 评委在投票前比较了两个设计各自的价值。
senses.why: Once merit means what is deserved, judging a thing on merit means setting aside the label and weighing what it can really do.
senses.whyCN: 既然 merit 指「应得之物」，那么按 merit 评判一事物，就是把招牌放到一边，只称量它真正能做到什么。

senses.title: A record that earns reward or honour
senses.definition: the accumulated record of good service or achievement that makes a person deserve reward, promotion or public honour
senses.definitionCN: 长期积累的良好服务或成绩，使人有资格获得奖赏、晋升或公开表彰
senses.example: Years of quiet merit finally brought her the senior post.
senses.exampleCN: 多年默默积累的功绩终于让她得到了那个高级职位。
senses.why: Because merit is something earned, it can be counted over time, and a long count of good work turns into the sense of service that a medal or a promotion answers.
senses.whyCN: 因为 merit 是挣来的东西，它可以随时间累积；长期积累的好工作就变成「功劳」这一层含义，奖章或晋升正是对它的回应。

senses.title: To deserve something
senses.definition: to be worth something, or to have earned attention, praise, punishment or serious consideration
senses.definitionCN: 够得上某物，或已经挣得注意、称赞、惩罚或认真对待的资格
senses.example: The question merits a careful answer rather than a quick guess.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题值得认真作答，而不该随手猜一句。
senses.why: The verb keeps the oldest Latin meaning almost untouched: merere was to earn, so to merit something is to have already earned it and therefore to deserve it.
senses.whyCN: 动词义几乎原样保留了拉丁语 merere 最古老的意思「挣得」：to merit 某物，就是已经把它挣到手，因此「值得」。

intro.en: Merit goes back to a Latin verb for earning, and the noun for the thing earned passed through French into English, where it became both a quality and a verb of deserving.
intro.cn: merit 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「挣得」的动词，指「挣得之物」的名词经法语进入英语，后来既是优点，也作「值得」的动词。

items.en: Merere meant to earn, to gain by service, and it already carried the idea that pay follows work.
items.cn: merere 意为挣得、靠出力获得，本身已带着「先有付出、后有回报」的意思。

items.en: Meritum was the noun for what had been earned or deserved, whether a wage, a reward or a good name.
items.cn: meritum 是名词，指挣得或应得的东西，可以是工钱、奖赏，也可以是好名声。

items.en: Old French took the Latin noun as merite, meaning worth, value or a deserving act, and used it in both praise and blame.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词写作 merite，意为价值、长处或值得称道的行为，褒贬两边都用。

items.en: Middle English merit named a quality worth praising and also the state of being entitled to a reward.
items.cn: 中古英语的 merit 既指值得称赞的品质，也指有资格获得奖赏的状态。

items.en: Modern English added the verb sense of deserving and kept the phrase on merit for judging without favour.
items.cn: 现代英语补上动词「值得」的用法，并保留 on merit 这一说法，指不带偏私地评判。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin earning family, including a prefixed word that reverses the value; the near-meaning group collects words for goodness and worth.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「挣得」词族，其中包括一个把价值反过来、加了前缀的词；近义组收表示良善与价值的词。

entries.definition: Deserving praise because of good work or service.
entries.definitionCN: 因出色的工作或贡献而值得称赞的。

entries.definition: A system in which power belongs to those who have earned it by ability.
entries.definitionCN: 权力归于凭才能挣得位置者的制度。

entries.definition: A fault or failing that counts against a person, the opposite of a merit.
entries.definitionCN: 记在人账上的缺点或过失，与优点相对。

entries.definition: Earned and therefore justly given, as of praise or punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 因挣得而应当给予的，用于称赞或惩罚。

entries.definition: A morally good quality in a person, especially one long practised.
entries.definitionCN: 人身上道德上的好品质，尤指长期养成的。

entries.definition: The true value of a thing, measured apart from its price or label.
entries.definitionCN: 事物真正的价值，不以价钱或标签衡量。

entries.definition: The importance or usefulness that something has for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 某物对某个用途的重要性或用处。

entries.definition: A quality a person or thing is good at, seen as a resource.
entries.definitionCN: 人或事物擅长的那一处品质，被看作可用的资源。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for earning; the family keeps returning to what is earned, what deserves praise and what can therefore be taken away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「挣得」的动词上，同族词反复回到挣得之物、值得称赞之处，以及因而已可被拿走的东西。

normal.en: Merere in Latin means to earn, so merit is not a gift but a balance built up by work.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merere 意为挣得，所以 merit 不是白送的礼，而是靠工作一点点攒出来的余额。

normal.en: Meritum is the thing earned, which is why the English noun can mean both a good quality and a record of service.
normal.cn: meritum 指挣得之物，所以英语名词既能指好品质，也能指功劳记录。

normal.en: Meritorious adds -orious and says a person or an act is full of merit.
normal.cn: meritorious 加 -orious，表示某人或某事充满 merit。

normal.en: Demerit adds de-, which takes value away, so the word names a fault instead of a virtue.
normal.cn: demerit 加 de-，把价值减掉，于是这个词指过失而不是美德。

normal.en: Meritocracy joins merit to -cracy, rule by those who have earned the right to rule.
normal.cn: meritocracy 把 merit 与 -cracy 组合，指由挣得统治资格者来统治。

abstract.en: A word for earned value suggests that praise is not something handed out but something a person has already paid for in effort.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「挣得价值」的词说明：称赞不是随手发的，而是人已经用力气付过账的。

abstract.en: Judging on merit asks a hard question, what would remain of this person if the name and the uniform were removed.
abstract.cn: 按 merit 评判要回答一个难题：若去掉姓名与制服，这个人还剩下什么。

abstract.en: Because merit can be counted and also taken away, the word quietly holds both fairness and the fear of losing it.
abstract.cn: 因为 merit 既能累积也能被扣掉，这个词同时装着公平，以及失去公平的忧虑。

examples.en: The panel judged the entries on merit alone.
examples.cn: 评审只看作品本身的长处。

examples.en: The proposal merits a second reading.
examples.cn: 这项提议值得再读一遍。

examples.en: Her merit was recognized long before the title arrived.
examples.cn: 早在头衔到来之前，她的功劳就已被看见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖力特」——肯卖力气的人特别值得称赞；记住 merit 是优点、值得。

root: 拉丁语 merere（挣得、应得）派生出 meritum（应得之物），经古法语 merite 进入英语；同族词多与功绩、应得、褒贬有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what has been earned and therefore deserves praise; the senses divide into a good quality, a thing's real worth, a record of service and the verb of deserving.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「挣得因而应得」；义项由此分出值得称赞的长处、事物本身的价值、功劳记录，以及动词「值得」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain work record lying open on a table, its long column of small entries outweighing the famous name on the cover.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊着一份朴素的工作记录，密密麻麻的小字压过了封面上那个显赫的姓氏。

branches.en: a quiet colleague whose steady work everyone trusts
branches.cn: 一位沉默的同事，靠稳定的工作赢得所有人的信任

branches.en: a plain design chosen over a glossy one
branches.cn: 朴素的设计胜过花哨的设计

branches.en: a judge weighing a plan with the price tag turned face down
branches.cn: 评审把价签翻过去，只称量方案本身

branches.en: a long service record read aloud at a ceremony
branches.cn: 典礼上被高声念出的一长串功绩记录

branches.en: a question that makes the whole room go quiet
branches.cn: 一个让全场安静下来的问题

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of earning, its noun for the thing earned, the French form, and English endings that build an adjective, a fault and a system.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示挣得的拉丁动词、指挣得之物的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词、过失词与制度词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 辐射；放射线；辐射热；散发
definition_en: energy that travels through space as waves or particles; the rays or particles themselves; heat transferred from a warm surface; the spreading of something outward from a centre
core_image: 一圈圈从中心向外扩散的细线，像热浪在空气里散开
scene: 实验室里，仪器旁贴着黄色警示牌，工作人员穿着厚重的防护服记录读数。 The meter showed a low level of radiation near the old mine.
sceneCN: 这里 radiation 是「辐射」（第 1 个义项：以波或粒子形式在空间传播的能量）；句意为仪器显示那座旧矿附近辐射水平很低。画面里可留意：黄色警示牌、厚重的防护服、跳动的读数。

pos.zh: 辐射；放射线；辐射热；散发

derivatives.zh: radiation 的动词形式，指发出辐射、从中心向外扩散
radiate 加 -or，指散发热量的暖气片或散热器
radiate 加 -ive，指与辐射有关的
同出拉丁语「射线」一词，指半径，即从中心射出的一条线

senses.title: Energy travelling as waves or particles
senses.definition: energy that moves through space in the form of waves or particles
senses.definitionCN: 以波或粒子形式在空间中传播的能量
senses.example: The sun's radiation warms the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳的辐射使地球变暖。
senses.why: Latin radiare meant to emit rays, and radiation names the whole process of energy going out in rays.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radiare 意为发出射线，radiation 指能量以射线形式向外发出的整个过程。

senses.title: The rays or particles themselves
senses.definition: the rays or particles produced by a source, considered as things in themselves
senses.definitionCN: 由某个源产生的射线或粒子，被当作事物本身来看
senses.example: Thick walls protected the workers from radiation.
senses.exampleCN: 厚墙保护工人免受放射线伤害。
senses.why: The process and its product share one noun, so the thing that travels is also called radiation.
senses.whyCN: 过程与产物共用一个名词，于是那些传播出去的东西也被称作 radiation。

senses.title: Heat given off by a warm surface
senses.definition: heat transferred from a warm object to cooler surroundings without moving air
senses.definitionCN: 热表面在不靠空气流动的情况下向较冷环境传递的热
senses.example: The radiator warms the room by radiation as well as by hot air.
senses.exampleCN: 暖气片既靠辐射也靠热空气使房间变暖。
senses.why: Physics divides heat transfer into conduction, convection and radiation, and the third name keeps the image of rays going out.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把传热分为传导、对流与辐射，第三个名称保留了「射线外发」的形象。

senses.title: A spreading outward from a centre
senses.definition: the spreading of something, such as ideas or influence, outward from a central point
senses.definitionCN: 思想或影响等从中心点向外扩散
senses.example: The radiation of new ideas across the region took decades.
senses.exampleCN: 新思想在该地区的扩散花了几十年。
senses.why: Anything that spreads outward like rays can be described with the same noun, even when nothing physical is travelling.
senses.whyCN: 任何像射线一样向外扩散的东西都能用这个名词描述，即使传播的并非实物。

intro.en: Radiation comes from a Latin verb meaning to emit rays, built on the Latin word for a spoke or a ray, and it entered English through the language of science.
intro.cn: radiation 源自一个意为「发出射线」的拉丁语动词，其基础是拉丁语表示「辐条、射线」的词，并经科学语言进入英语。

items.en: Radius meant a spoke of a wheel or a ray of light, a straight line going out from a centre.
items.cn: radius 指车轮的辐条或一束光线，是从中心射出的一条直线。

items.en: Radiare meant to send out rays or to shine, describing light leaving a source in straight lines.
items.cn: radiare 意为发出射线或发光，描述光从光源沿直线射出。

items.en: Radiatio named the act of shining or the rays sent out, and it was used for the glow of a source.
items.cn: radiatio 指发光这一行为或发出的射线，曾用来指光源的光辉。

items.en: Scientists applied the word to energy leaving a body in waves or particles, and English adopted that use.
items.cn: 科学家把这个词用于物体以波或粒子形式放出的能量，英语接受了这一用法。

items.en: Modern English uses radiation for nuclear and solar energy, for the rays themselves, for radiant heat and for any outward spread.
items.cn: 现代英语用 radiation 指核能与太阳能、射线本身、辐射热，以及任何向外扩散。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the Latin stem of rays; the near-meaning group gathers words for emitted energy and outflow.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「射线」词干上的形式；近义组收表示发出的能量与外流的词。

entries.definition: To send out rays, heat or a feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 发出射线、热或某种感觉。

entries.definition: A device that gives off heat into a room.
entries.definitionCN: 向房间散发热量的装置。

entries.definition: Relating to the giving off of rays.
A straight line from the centre to the edge of a circle.
entries.definitionCN: 从圆心到圆周的一条直线。

entries.definition: The act of sending something out.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物发送出去的行为。

entries.definition: A narrow beam of light or energy.
The capacity to do work or to cause change.
entries.definitionCN: 做功或引起变化的能力。

entries.definition: Radioactive particles that settle after an explosion.
entries.definitionCN: 爆炸后落下的放射性颗粒。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the image of a spoke or a ray leaving a centre, and every sense keeps that picture of something going outward.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在「从中心射出的辐条或光线」这一意象上，每个义项都保留了「向外而去」的画面。

normal.en: Radiation, radius and radiate all come from the Latin word for a ray, a line leaving a centre.
normal.cn: radiation、radius 与 radiate 都出自拉丁语表示射线的词，即从中心射出的一条线。

normal.en: A radiator heats a room by giving off rays of warmth, which is why it shares the name.
normal.cn: 暖气片靠散发热射线来温暖房间，所以它共用这个名字。

normal.en: Nuclear radiation is invisible, so people measure it with counters rather than with their senses.
normal.cn: 核辐射看不见，所以人们用计数器而不是感官来测量它。

normal.en: Radiation therapy uses controlled rays to treat illness, turning the same energy into a tool.
normal.cn: 放射治疗用受控的射线治病，把同一种能量变成工具。

normal.en: The radiation of ideas is a metaphor: nothing physical travels, but influence spreads like light.
normal.cn: 思想的扩散是比喻：没有实物在旅行，但影响像光一样传播。

abstract.en: A word built from spokes reminds us that every source sends something outward, whether heat, light or fear.
abstract.cn: 一个由辐条构成的词提醒我们：每个源头都在向外发送什么，无论是热、光还是恐惧。

abstract.en: Radiation is both a danger and a cure, and the same noun names the healer and the threat.
abstract.cn: 辐射既是危险也是治疗手段，同一个名词既指救治之物，也指威胁。

abstract.en: What spreads from a centre cannot be recalled, which is why the word carries a quiet sense of consequence.
abstract.cn: 从中心扩散出去的东西收不回来，所以这个词带着一种无声的「后果」意味。

examples.en: Thin clouds do not stop all of the sun's radiation.
examples.cn: 薄云并不能挡住太阳的全部辐射。

examples.en: Workers at the plant wear badges that measure radiation.
examples.cn: 工厂的工人佩戴测量辐射的徽章。

examples.en: The radiation of the new style reached neighbouring towns within a few years.
examples.cn: 这种新风格的扩散在几年内就传到了邻近城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐地埃申」——锐利的东西从一点向四面射出，记住 radiation 是辐射。

root: 拉丁语 radius（辐条、射线）→ radiare（发出射线）→ radiatio（发光、射线）→ 英语 radiation；同族有 radiate、radiator、radiative、radius。

sensesIntro.en: The core is rays leaving a centre; the senses divide into the energy, the rays themselves, radiant heat and any outward spreading.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「从中心射出的线」；义项分为能量、射线本身、辐射热，以及任何向外的扩散。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fine lines spreading outward from a single point, like heat shimmering off a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一个点向外散开的细线，像热浪从表面升腾。

branches.en: a sunlit stone warming in the open
branches.cn: 露天里被晒热的石头

branches.en: a badge worn to measure what cannot be seen
branches.cn: 为测量看不见之物而佩戴的徽章

branches.en: a radiator ticking as it heats a room
branches.cn: 暖气片发出轻响、温暖房间

branches.en: a style spreading from one town to the next
branches.cn: 从一座城传到下一座城的风格

branches.en: the same outward flow of heat, once from the sun and once from a pipe
branches.cn: 同一种向外的热流，一次来自太阳，一次来自管道

intro.en: The word is Latin throughout: a noun of rays, a verb of sending them out and a noun of action, with English relatives built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都是拉丁语：表示射线的名词、表示发出射线的动词与动作名词，加上由同一词干构成的英语亲属词。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius also gave English radius, the line from the centre of a circle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 radius 还给英语送来了 radius，即从圆心射出的一条线。

definition_zh: 陡峭地；急剧地；大幅地
definition_en: at a sharp angle, or by a large and sudden amount
core_image: 一条曲线像墙一样陡然冲高
scene: 价格急剧上涨。 Prices rose steeply.
sceneCN: 这里 steeply 是「急剧地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：价格急剧上涨。

senses.title: At a sharp angle
senses.definition: in a way that rises or falls at a sharp angle
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的角度上升或下降地
senses.example: The path climbs steeply.
senses.exampleCN: 小路陡峭地向上延伸。
senses.why: This is the literal slope sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的坡度义项。

senses.title: By a large amount
senses.definition: by a large and sudden amount
senses.definitionCN: 以很大且突然的幅度
senses.example: Prices rose steeply.
senses.exampleCN: 价格急剧上涨。
senses.why: A steep line on a chart moves steeply.
senses.whyCN: 图表上陡的线，就是急剧地变化。

senses.title: At a tilt
senses.definition: in a slanted or sloping position
senses.definitionCN: 以倾斜或斜面的姿态
senses.example: The roof slopes steeply to the north.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶向北陡斜。
senses.why: The angle sense narrowed to a tilt.
senses.whyCN: 角度义收窄为倾斜。

intro.en: Steeply is steep plus the adverb ending -ly, built in modern English.
intro.cn: steeply 是 steep 加副词后缀 -ly，在现代英语中构成。

items.en: Steap meant lofty or deep.
items.cn: steap 意为高耸或深陷。

items.en: Steep named a sharp slope.
items.cn: steep 指陡坡。

items.en: The suffix -ly formed the adverb steeply.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 steeply。

items.en: Steeply spread to prices and numbers.
items.cn: steeply 扩展到价格与数字。

items.en: It now describes any sharp change.
items.cn: 它现在描述任何急剧的变化。

note.en: Steeply is compared with look-alike words and with adverbs of sharp change.
note.cn: 把 steeply 与形近词以及表示剧变的副词作比较。

entries.definition: rising sharply
to a great depth
a church tower
suddenly and by a lot
very quickly
suddenly and without warning

normalIntro.en: Steeply turns an angle into motion: a path climbs, a price jumps, a roof leans.
normalIntro.cn: steeply 把角度变成动作：路在攀升，价在跳涨，屋顶在倾斜。

normal.en: The road rises steeply here.
normal.cn: 这条路在这里陡升。

normal.en: Sales fell steeply last year.
normal.cn: 去年销量急剧下降。

normal.en: The hill slopes steeply to the river.
normal.cn: 山坡向河边陡斜。

normal.en: House prices climbed steeply.
normal.cn: 房价急剧攀升。

normal.en: The steps go up steeply.
normal.cn: 台阶陡峭地向上。

abstract.en: A steep line is a promise and a warning at once.
abstract.cn: 陡峭的曲线，既是承诺也是警告。

abstract.en: What rises steeply can fall the same way.
abstract.cn: 陡升的东西，也能陡落。

abstract.en: The angle shows how little time there is.
abstract.cn: 角度大小，透露出时间还剩多少。

examples.en: Prices rose steeply.
examples.cn: 价格急剧上涨。

examples.en: The path climbs steeply.
examples.cn: 小路陡峭地向上延伸。

examples.en: The roof slopes steeply to the north.
examples.cn: 屋顶向北陡斜。

dict_mnemonic.text: steeply 是 steep 加 -ly，本指「陡峭地」，用于价格、数量时常译「急剧地」，rise steeply 与 fall steeply 是最常见搭配。

root: steep（陡的）加副词后缀 -ly；由坡度陡峭引申为数量、价格变动的急剧。

sensesIntro.en: Steeply means at a sharp angle, by a sharp amount, or in a slanted position.
sensesIntro.cn: steeply 指以陡的角度、以急剧的幅度，或以倾斜的姿态。

core.en: A line that climbs like a wall.
core.cn: 一条像墙一样上升的线。

branches.en: A trail leans into a hillside.
branches.cn: 小径斜插进山坡。

branches.en: A number on a screen jumps upward.
branches.cn: 屏幕上的数字向上跳。

branches.en: A roof tilts away from the rain.
branches.cn: 屋顶斜着让雨流走。

branches.en: Both a path and a roof keep the same angle.
branches.cn: 小径与屋顶，保持着同一个角度。

branches.en: A slanted line can also be a risky graph.
branches.cn: 倾斜的线，也可能是一条危险的曲线。

intro.en: Steeply is fixed in form, built from steep and -ly.
intro.cn: steeply 形式固定，由 steep 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: The steepness is measured in degrees.
The grain is steeped in water.
The steeple stands on the hill.

definition_zh: 侦探；警探；侦探的
definition_en: a person, especially a police officer, whose job is to investigate crimes
core_image: 台灯下摊开的卷宗，旁边是一枚装进小纸袋的纽扣
scene: 雨夜的小办公室里，男人按灭烟头，翻开一叠照片。 The detective studied the photographs until dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 detective 指「侦探」（第 1 个义项：专门查案的人）；句意是那名侦探研究照片直到天亮。

senses.title: A person who solves crimes
senses.definition: a person whose job is to find out who committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 以查明谁犯了罪为职业的人
senses.example: The detective questioned every neighbour on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 那名侦探询问了街上的每一位邻居。
senses.why: Someone has to stand between a quiet lie and the truth.
senses.whyCN: 总得有人站在安静的谎言与真相之间。

senses.title: A police investigator
senses.definition: a police officer who collects evidence and follows a case to its end
senses.definitionCN: 收集证据并把案件追到最后的警察
senses.example: A police detective arrived with a thin notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 一位警探带着薄薄的笔记本到了。
senses.why: The same curiosity now wears a badge and follows rules.
senses.whyCN: 同一种好奇心，如今戴上了警徽，也守着规矩。

senses.title: Relating to crime solving
senses.definition: used to describe stories, work or methods connected with solving crimes
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容与查案有关的故事、工作或方法
senses.example: She reads detective novels on the long train ride.
senses.exampleCN: 她在漫长的火车旅途中读侦探小说。
senses.why: The noun lent its name to the shelf it fills.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把自己的名字借给了摆满它的书架。

intro.en: Detective was built inside English from detect plus -ive, and detect itself goes back to Latin detegere, to uncover.
intro.cn: detective 是在英语内部由 detect 加 -ive 造出来的，而 detect 又可追到拉丁语 detegere（揭开）。

items.en: Detegere joined de-, away, to tegere, to cover, and meant to uncover.
items.cn: detegere 把 de-（去掉）与 tegere（覆盖）拼在一起，意思是揭开。

items.en: Detect entered English as a verb meaning to expose what was hidden.
items.cn: detect 作为动词进入英语，指把隐藏的东西揭出来。

items.en: Britain coined detective for the new plain-clothes police.
items.cn: 英国为新出现的便衣警察造出了 detective 这个词。

items.en: Cheap magazines made the detective a hero of popular fiction.
items.cn: 廉价杂志让侦探成了通俗小说里的英雄。

items.en: The word now covers police officers and private investigators alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词既指警察，也指私人调查者。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the detect stem, and the meaning group names different kinds of people who follow clues.
note.cn: 形近组共用 detect 这个词干，近义组则给出几种循线索查案的人。

entries.definition: to notice or uncover something
the act of finding something hidden
a device that senses something
a person who examines facts carefully
a police officer of higher rank
a person who follows clues

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a lamp over an open file and end with a stranger asking quiet questions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从照着摊开卷宗的台灯开始，落到轻声问话的陌生人。

normal.en: Detect plus -ive simply gives you the person who does the detecting.
normal.cn: detect 加上 -ive，就是做探查的那个人。

normal.en: A detective reads a room the way others read a page.
normal.cn: 侦探读一间屋子的方式，就像别人读一页纸。

normal.en: The coat is ordinary; only the questions are sharp.
normal.cn: 外套很普通，只有问题很锋利。

normal.en: Every clue is a sentence still waiting for its verb.
normal.cn: 每条线索都是一句还在等动词的话。

normal.en: Private or police, the job is the same: assemble the truth.
normal.cn: 私人也好，警察也好，活儿一样：把真相拼起来。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp with a green glass shade.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏罩着绿玻璃的台灯。

abstract.en: Picture a row of paper bags, each holding one small object.
abstract.cn: 想象一排纸袋，每只装着一件小东西。

abstract.en: Picture a hand drawing a line between two names.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在两个名字之间画一条线。

examples.en: The detective questioned every neighbour on the street.
examples.cn: 那名侦探询问了街上的每一位邻居。

examples.en: She hired a private detective to find her brother.
examples.cn: 她雇了一名私人侦探去找她的弟弟。

examples.en: Detective stories sell well at the station bookshop.
examples.cn: 侦探小说在车站书店卖得很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 detective 记成「地泰克提夫」：de 是去掉，tect 是盖子，-ive 指人，专门把盖子掀开的人就是侦探。

root: 由英语动词 detect 加后缀 -ive 构成，而 detect 来自拉丁语 detegere（揭开覆盖物）。十九世纪英国为便衣警察造出这个词，后来既指警探，也指私人侦探，并引申出「侦探的」这一形容词用法。

sensesIntro.en: From a person who uncovers, to a police officer on a case, to the stories told about both.
sensesIntro.cn: 从揭开真相的人，到办案的警察，再到关于他们的故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp, a file and one small object sealed in a paper bag.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏台灯、一份卷宗，以及纸袋里封着的一件小东西。

branches.en: The first sense is the person who does the assembling.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是做这次拼合的人。

branches.en: The second sense gives that person a badge.
branches.cn: 第二个义项给这个人一枚警徽。

branches.en: The third sense is the shelf of stories about such work.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是关于这类工作的那一架故事书。

branches.en: A private eye and a police officer share one method.
branches.cn: 私人侦探与警察共用一套方法。

branches.en: The worker and the fiction about the worker grew up together.
branches.cn: 真实的人与写他的小说是一起长大的。

intro.en: Detective belongs to a small family built on the act of uncovering.
intro.cn: detective 属于一小族词，都建在「揭开」这个动作上。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Latin tegere, to cover, and de- turns covering into uncovering.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是拉丁语 tegere（覆盖），前缀 de- 把覆盖变成揭开。

items.example: The detective waited outside the door.

items.exampleCN: 仪器能察觉微弱的信号。

items.example: Detection came too late to help.
items.exampleCN: 发现来得太晚，已经无济于事。
这种变化几乎察觉不到。
他悄无声息地溜了进去。
两名侦探共同负责这个案子。

definition_zh: 接受；认可；容忍；承兑
definition_en: the act of receiving something, approving of it, or bearing it
core_image: 一双手从对面接过一份文件，随即在末尾签下名字
scene: 招聘会上，她接过录用通知，在签名栏写下自己的名字。 Her acceptance of the offer came within a minute.
sceneCN: 这里的 acceptance 指「接受」（第 1 个义项：同意接收别人给出的东西）；句意是她在一分钟内就接受了这份工作。

pos.zh: 接受；认可；容忍；（票据）承兑

senses.title: Receiving what is offered
senses.definition: the act of agreeing to take something that is offered
senses.definitionCN: 同意收下别人递来的东西
senses.example: Her acceptance of the offer came within a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一分钟内就接受了这份工作。
senses.why: The Latin verb accipere is built from ad-, towards, and capere, to take, so the noun first names the taking of something held out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 accipere 由 ad-（朝向）与 capere（拿取）组成，所以这个名词最初就指「把递到面前的东西收下」。

senses.title: Approval by others
senses.definition: the state of being approved of or believed by a group
senses.definitionCN: 被一群人认同或相信的状态
senses.example: The theory slowly gained acceptance among physicists.
senses.exampleCN: 这一理论逐渐获得物理学界的认可。
senses.why: Once a person takes an idea in, the idea is treated as his own; that inner taking became public approval.
senses.whyCN: 人把一种说法收进心里之后就会把它当成自己的，这种「收进来」就发展成了公开的认可。

senses.title: Bearing a hard situation
senses.definition: willingness to bear a difficult situation that cannot be changed
senses.definitionCN: 愿意承受无法改变的困难处境
senses.example: His calm acceptance of the loss impressed everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静地接受损失，让所有人都很佩服。
senses.why: A loss cannot be handed back, yet people still take it in, and that reluctant taking is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 损失退不回去，人却仍旧把它收进生活里，这份不情愿的收下就是「容忍」这一义项。

senses.title: Agreeing to pay a bill
senses.definition: a bank's formal promise to pay a bill of exchange
senses.definitionCN: 银行对汇票作出的正式付款承诺
senses.example: The bank's acceptance of the draft made the deal possible.
senses.exampleCN: 银行承兑了这张汇票，交易才得以完成。
senses.why: In trade the bank receives the draft and promises to honour it, which is the commercial branch of taking something in.
senses.whyCN: 在贸易中银行收下汇票并承诺付款，正是「收下」这个动作在商业里的专门用法。

intro.en: The word is a noun of taking, formed from a Latin verb that joined towards with to seize.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「拿取」的名词，来自一个由「朝向」与「抓住」拼成的拉丁动词。

items.en: capere meant to take or seize.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取、抓住。

items.en: accipere added ad-, towards, and meant to receive.
items.cn: accipere 加上 ad-（朝向），意为接收。

items.en: acceptare stressed the repeated or willing side of receiving.
items.cn: acceptare 强调接收中反复、乐意的成分。

items.en: acceptance named the act of receiving favourably.
items.cn: acceptance 指欣然接收的行为。

items.en: the word entered English with both the personal and the legal sense.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语时，既带个人层面的含义，也带法律层面的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accept family; the near-meaning group names approval and endurance.
note.cn: 形近组是 accept 词族；近义组表示认可与承受。

entries.definition: to take what is offered
good enough to be agreed to
in a way that can be agreed to
willing to take things as they are
a favourable opinion of something
public respect for an achievement
permission for something to happen
the ability to bear something difficult
the act of starting to use an idea or method

normalIntro.en: These hints follow capere, the Latin verb for taking hold.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着拉丁语里表示「拿住」的 capere。

normal.en: capere is to take, and acceptance is the taking of what is held out.
normal.cn: capere 是拿取，acceptance 就是接过别人递来的东西。

normal.en: the -ance ending turns the verb accept into a noun of action.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ance 把动词 accept 变成表示动作的名词。

normal.en: a theory wins acceptance only after many people take it in.
normal.cn: 一种理论要许多人把它收进心里，才算获得认可。

normal.en: acceptance of a loss is taking in what cannot be returned.
normal.cn: 接受损失，就是把退不回去的东西收进生活。

normal.en: in banking the draft is received, so the promise to pay is an acceptance.
normal.cn: 银行收下汇票，所以付款承诺也叫 acceptance。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope changing hands and a signature appearing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个信封换了手，签名随之出现。

abstract.en: See a crowd slowly nodding at a new idea.
abstract.cn: 想象人群对着一个新想法慢慢点头。

abstract.en: Think of a heavy box set down on the floor and accepted as part of the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的箱子被放到地上，从此留在房间里。

examples.en: Her acceptance of the offer came within a minute.
examples.cn: 她一分钟内就接受了这份工作。

examples.en: The new method has won wide acceptance in schools.
examples.cn: 这种新方法在学校里获得了广泛认可。

examples.en: He showed quiet acceptance of the news.
examples.cn: 他平静地接受了这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: accept（接受）加上名词后缀 -ance，把「收下」这个动作本身变成名词。

root: 拉丁语 accipere（接收）：ad-（朝向）+ capere（拿取），加 -ance 构成名词，本义「收下」，引申为认可、容忍与票据承兑。

sensesIntro.en: One noun of taking runs from a signed offer through public approval to a bank's promise and a patient endurance.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示「收下」的名词，从签下的录用通知一路走到公众认可、银行承诺与默默承受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an offered paper taken in hand and signed.
core.cn: 核心意象：递来的文件被接住并签名。

branches.en: a letter or offer received and kept
branches.cn: 被接下并留存的信件或提议

branches.en: an idea taken in by a whole field
branches.cn: 被整个领域接纳的想法

branches.en: a loss taken into one's life without protest
branches.cn: 被默默收进生活的损失

branches.en: a draft received by a bank with a promise to pay
branches.cn: 被银行收下并承诺付款的汇票

branches.en: the same taking, first of an object and then of a belief
branches.cn: 同一种「收下」，先收物件，再收信念

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of taking plus a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「拿取」动词加名词词尾构成的。

latinIntro.en: The root capere, to take, also gives capture, captive and capacity.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 capere（拿取）还给出 capture、captive 与 capacity。

definition_zh: 唤醒；使醒来；醒来；觉醒
definition_en: to wake, or to make someone wake, especially in a formal or literary way
core_image: 一只手轻轻碰肩，睡着的人慢慢睁开眼睛
scene: 清晨的营地里，领队沿着帐篷一个个走过，轻声把大家叫起来。 He was wakened by the sound of the gate opening.
sceneCN: 这里 waken 是「被唤醒」（第 1 个义项：使从睡眠中醒来）；句意为大门开动的声音把他弄醒了。有人轻碰肩膀、睡者慢慢睁眼，正是这个词的形象。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -en 得到的短形，义为「醒来；唤醒」
a- 与 wake 同源，义为「醒着的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「觉醒；唤醒」

senses.title: To make someone wake
senses.definition: to cause a sleeping person to wake, often by sound or touch
senses.definitionCN: 通过声音或触碰使睡着的人醒来
senses.example: He was wakened by the sound of the gate opening.
senses.exampleCN: 大门开启的声音把他弄醒了。
senses.why: Old English had weccan for waking another; adding -en made a regular verb from the same idea, still slightly formal today.
senses.whyCN: 古英语本有 weccan 表示叫醒别人，加上 -en 从同一想法造出规则动词，至今仍略偏正式。

senses.title: To wake oneself
senses.definition: to come out of sleep, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 不带宾语时表示自己从睡中醒来
senses.example: She wakened before the light and listened to the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前她醒来，听着鸟叫。
senses.why: The suffixed verb works both ways, so the same form turns to the sleeper as subject.
senses.whyCN: 带后缀的动词两边都通，同一形式也可以让睡者作主语。

senses.title: To stir a feeling or a memory
senses.definition: to bring a feeling or a memory back into active thought
senses.definitionCN: 使某种感情或记忆重新回到意识中
senses.example: The old song wakened memories of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 那首老歌唤起了对村庄的记忆。
senses.why: Waking a person and waking a memory are the same act of setting something asleep into motion.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫醒与把记忆叫醒是同一个动作：让睡着的东西重新动起来。

senses.title: To come to awareness
senses.definition: to become aware of a situation, especially something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 意识到某种状况，尤其是不对劲的状况
senses.example: The village was wakened to the danger of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 全村终于意识到这条河的危险。
senses.why: The formal verb suits public statements, so it carries the sense of slow collective awareness better than wake.
senses.whyCN: 正式动词适合公共表述，因此比 wake 更能表达缓慢的集体觉醒。

senses.title: To rouse activity
senses.definition: to cause something dormant to become active again
senses.definitionCN: 使沉寂之物重新活跃起来
senses.example: The new market wakened trade in the small town.
senses.exampleCN: 新市场让这座小镇的贸易活了起来。
senses.why: From people the verb reaches anything that can sleep or stir, such as trade, interest or a quiet street.
senses.whyCN: 从人可以推到任何能「睡着」或「动弹」的事物，如贸易、兴趣或安静的街道。

intro.en: Waken is wake plus the old verb ending -en, which makes a verb from a verb without changing the meaning.
intro.cn: waken 是 wake 加古动词词尾 -en，由动词造出动词，而意义不变。

items.en: Wacan meant to wake and weccan meant to wake another.
items.cn: wacan 意为醒来，weccan 意为叫醒别人。

items.en: The -en ending was added in the Middle English period to make a regular form.
items.cn: 中古英语时期加上 -en 词尾，构成规则形式。

items.en: The new verb avoided the awkward past wook and spread quickly in writing.
items.cn: 新动词避开了别扭的过去式 wook，很快在书面语中流行。

items.en: Later English preferred wake with up for speech and waken for formal prose.
items.cn: 此后英语口语多用 wake up，正式散文多用 waken。

items.en: The figurative senses of memory and awareness came with the formal register.
items.cn: 记忆与觉悟的比喻义随正式语体一并出现。

note.en: The first group holds the wake family, the second the near synonyms with their differences.
note.cn: 第一组收 wake 词族，第二组收近义词及彼此的差别。

entries.definition: The third person singular form.
The past tense and past participle.
The shorter everyday verb, with woke and woken.
entries.definitionCN: 更短的日常动词，过去式与过去分词为 woke、woken。

entries.definition: A near twin, slightly more literary.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎同义，更具文学色彩。

entries.definition: To wake someone, often with effort or by shaking.
Chiefly to stir a feeling or a reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 主要表示激起感情或反应。

entries.definition: To move lightly or to begin to feel something.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻动一下，或开始有某种感受。

entries.definition: To warn someone so that they are ready.

normalIntro.en: Add -en to a short verb and it becomes formal: waken, broaden, deepen.
normalIntro.cn: 给短动词加 -en 会变得正式：waken、broaden、deepen 都是如此。

normal.en: Waken is regular: waken, wakened, wakened.
normal.cn: waken 是规则动词：waken、wakened、wakened。

normal.en: Awaken and waken are near twins; awaken is more literary.
normal.cn: awaken 与 waken 近似孪生，awaken 更具文学味。

normal.en: Waken can take an object or stand alone.
normal.cn: waken 既可带宾语，也可单独使用。

normal.en: The -en ending also appears in broaden and deepen.
normal.cn: -en 词尾也见于 broaden、deepen。

normal.en: Waken interest and waken memories use the same stirring idea.
normal.cn: waken interest 与 waken memories 用的是同一种「唤起」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a shoulder early in the morning.
abstract.cn: 想清晨一只手轻轻落在肩上。

abstract.en: Hear a gate swing open and a sleeper sit up.
abstract.cn: 听大门开动，睡着的人坐了起来。

abstract.en: Feel an old song bringing a whole village back.
abstract.cn: 感受一首老歌把整个村庄带回来。

examples.en: The birds wakened him long before sunrise.
examples.cn: 日出之前很久，鸟叫声就把他弄醒了。

examples.en: She wakened slowly, unsure of the room.
examples.cn: 她慢慢醒来，一时认不清这间屋子。

examples.en: The letter wakened old fears.
examples.cn: 这封信唤起了旧日的恐惧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂肯」——喂，肯，快肯睁眼，天亮该起了。

root: wake（古英语 wacan / weccan，醒来、唤醒）+ 古动词词尾 -en → waken；同族词有 awaken、wakeful。

sensesIntro.en: One suffixed verb stretches from a shoulder touched in the dark to a village waking to danger.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个带后缀的动词从暗里被碰到的肩膀，一直伸到意识到危险的全村。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a shoulder and slowly opening eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：手落在肩上，眼睛慢慢睁开。

branches.en: The rousing branch: wakened by a gate.
branches.cn: 唤醒分支：被大门声弄醒。

branches.en: The self-waking branch: waking before the light.
branches.cn: 自醒分支：天亮前醒来。

branches.en: The memory branch: an old song waking memories.
branches.cn: 记忆分支：老歌唤起回忆。

branches.en: The awareness branch: a village waking to a river's danger.
branches.cn: 觉悟分支：全村意识到河流的危险。

branches.en: The activity branch: a market waking trade.
branches.cn: 活跃分支：市场让贸易活起来。

intro.en: Wak- is the wake root and -en is the old verb-making ending; the rest is plain English.
intro.cn: wak- 是 wake 词根，-en 是古老的造动词词尾，其余都是普通英语变化。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; no Latin form belongs to it, so the entry lists none.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语，没有对应的拉丁形式，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The root carries the waking act.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「醒」的动作。

items.example: One can waken an interest again.

definition_zh: 缺点；不足；短板
definition_en: a fault or weakness in a person, plan, or thing
core_image: 一面镜子上有一道细细的裂纹，正好照出人影的缺口
scene: 每个人都有缺点，重要的是改正。 Everyone has shortcomings; what matters is fixing them.
sceneCN: 这里 shortcoming 是「缺点」（第 1 个义项）；句意：每个人都有缺点，重要的是改正。

senses.title: A personal fault
senses.definition: a fault in someone's character or ability
senses.definitionCN: 性格或能力上的缺陷
senses.example: Everyone has shortcomings; what matters is fixing them.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都有缺点，重要的是改正。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的现代义项。

senses.title: A weakness in a plan
senses.definition: a weakness in a plan, system, or product
senses.definitionCN: 计划、系统或产品中的弱点
senses.example: The report lists the plan's shortcomings.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了计划的不足之处。
senses.why: The same word names flaws in things.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指事物的缺陷。

senses.title: A weak point
senses.definition: a part that falls below the rest
senses.definitionCN: 低于其余部分的一环
senses.example: Training is the team's biggest shortcoming.
senses.exampleCN: 训练是这支队伍最大的短板。
senses.why: A shortcoming is a place that comes up short.
senses.whyCN: 缺点就是达不到要求的地方。

intro.en: Shortcoming comes from the phrase to come short, to fail to reach.
intro.cn: shortcoming 来自短语 come short，意为达不到。

items.en: Sceort and cuman meant short and come.
items.cn: sceort 与 cuman 分别是短和来。

items.en: Come short meant fail to reach a mark.
items.cn: come short 意为未达到目标。

items.en: Shortcoming named a failure or defect.
items.cn: shortcoming 指失败或缺陷。

items.en: Shortcoming became common in reviews.
items.cn: shortcoming 在评论中变得常见。

items.en: The plural often means personal weaknesses.
items.cn: 复数常指个人缺点。

note.en: Shortcoming is compared with similar-looking words and with words for faults.
note.cn: 把 shortcoming 与形近词以及表示缺点的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small list of chosen candidates
fast writing with symbols
a baseball fielding position
a lack of strength or a fault
a mistake or defect
a fault in something

normalIntro.en: A shortcoming is the place where you come up short.
normalIntro.cn: shortcoming 就是你「差一点」的地方。

normal.en: Patience is not my shortcoming.
normal.cn: 耐心不是我的缺点。

normal.en: The plan has serious shortcomings.
normal.cn: 这个计划有严重不足。

normal.en: She knows her shortcomings.
normal.cn: 她了解自己的缺点。

normal.en: We must overcome these shortcomings.
normal.cn: 我们必须克服这些缺点。

normal.en: The review points out one obvious shortcoming.
normal.cn: 评论指出了一个明显不足。

abstract.en: A shortcoming is a door that opens inward.
abstract.cn: 缺点是朝内开的门。

abstract.en: Knowing your faults is the first repair.
abstract.cn: 认识缺点是第一次修理。

abstract.en: Every strength casts a shortcoming as its shadow.
abstract.cn: 每种长处都投下缺点的影子。

examples.en: Everyone has shortcomings; what matters is fixing them.
examples.cn: 每个人都有缺点，重要的是改正。

examples.en: The report lists the plan's shortcomings.
examples.cn: 报告列出了计划的不足之处。

examples.en: Training is the team's biggest shortcoming.
examples.cn: 训练是这支队伍最大的短板。

dict_mnemonic.text: shortcoming 就是「come short」（差一点没达到）变来的：达不到标准的地方，就是缺点。

root: 由 short 与 coming 复合，源出短语 come short（未达到），核心义「不足之处」。

sensesIntro.en: Shortcoming means a personal fault, a weakness in a plan, or a weak point.
sensesIntro.cn: shortcoming 意为缺点、不足或短板。

core.en: A place that falls short of what is needed.
core.cn: 达不到要求的那个地方。

branches.en: A personal habit that fails.
branches.cn: 失败的个人习惯。

branches.en: A plan with a gap.
branches.cn: 有漏洞的计划。

branches.en: One part weaker than the rest.
branches.cn: 比其余部分弱的一环。

branches.en: People and plans can both fall short.
branches.cn: 人和计划都可能不达标。

branches.en: A gap in a system is a weak point.
branches.cn: 系统中的缺口就是短板。

intro.en: Shortcoming forms a small family of fault words.
intro.cn: shortcoming 形成一个表示缺点的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shortcoming is Germanic; Latin defectus, failure, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shortcoming 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 defectus（失败）只是语义对应词。

items.example: Honesty about a shortcoming builds trust.
The result came short of the goal.
The plan came short of expectations.

items.meaning: a failure to reach an amount

items.example: The fault lies in the design.

items.exampleCN: 没有计划是毫无缺点的。

definition_zh: 生物学；（某地区的）生物
definition_en: the study of living things, or the living things of a place
core_image: 显微镜下缓缓移动的细胞
scene: 显微镜下，细胞在缓慢移动。 She studies biology at university.
sceneCN: 这里 biology 是「生物学」（第 1 个义项：研究生物的科学）；句意是她在大学学习生物学。

derivatives.zh: 由 biology 加 -ist 构成，义为「生物学家」
由 biology 加 -ical 构成，义为「生物的」
由 biological 加 -ally 构成，义为「在生物学上」

senses.title: The science of living things
senses.definition: the scientific study of living things
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物的科学
senses.example: She studies biology at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学习生物学。
senses.why: The Greek roots mean the study of life.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根的意思就是「关于生命的研究」。

senses.title: Living things of a place
senses.definition: the living things found in an area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区生活的生物
senses.example: The biology of the lake is very rich.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖的生物非常丰富。
senses.why: The name of the science also names its subject matter.
senses.whyCN: 学科之名也用来指它研究的对象。

intro.en: Biology joins Greek bios, life, and -logy, study.
intro.cn: biology 由希腊语 bios（生命）与 -logy（研究）合成。

items.en: bios meant life.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命」。

items.en: logos meant word or reason.
items.cn: logos 意为「言说、道理」。

items.en: biology named the science of life.
items.cn: biology 成为研究生命的学科名。

items.en: biology split into many branches.
items.cn: 生物学分出许多分支。

items.en: biology also means local living things.
items.cn: 如今 biology 也指一地的生物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ology ending; the near-meaning group gives life-science words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -ology 收尾；近义组是生命科学相关词。

entries.definition: the story of a person's life
the study of rocks
the study of living systems
the study of plants
the study of animals
organised knowledge of the world

normalIntro.en: Biology is bio, life, plus logy, study.
normalIntro.cn: biology 就是 bio（生命）加 logy（研究）。

normal.en: Biology is uncountable as a subject.
normal.cn: 作学科时 biology 不可数。

normal.en: A biologist works in biology.
normal.cn: biologist 从事生物学研究。

normal.en: The adjective is biological.
normal.cn: 形容词是 biological。

normal.en: Marine biology studies sea life.
normal.cn: marine biology 研究海洋生物。

normal.en: The -logy ending signals a field of study.
normal.cn: 词尾 -logy 表示一门学问。

abstract.en: See cells drifting under a microscope.
abstract.cn: 想象显微镜下漂移的细胞。

abstract.en: See a leaf held up to the light.
abstract.cn: 想象举向光线的叶片。

abstract.en: See a notebook filled with sketches of insects.
abstract.cn: 想象画满昆虫的笔记本。

examples.en: She studies biology at university.
examples.cn: 她在大学学习生物学。

examples.en: The biology of the lake is very rich.
examples.cn: 这个湖的生物非常丰富。

examples.en: Molecular biology has advanced quickly.
examples.cn: 分子生物学发展得很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio 是「生命」，logy 是「学问」，研究生命的学问就是生物学。

root: 由希腊语 bios（生命）与 -logia（研究）合成，十九世纪初成为学科名称，二十世纪分裂出分子生物学等分支，也用于指一地的生物。

sensesIntro.en: The science and the living matter it studies share one name.
sensesIntro.cn: 这门学科与它所研究的活物共用一个名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cells drifting under a microscope.
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下漂移的细胞。

branches.en: study biology
branches.cn: 学习生物学

branches.en: marine biology
branches.cn: 海洋生物学

branches.en: molecular biology
branches.cn: 分子生物学

branches.en: the biology of the lake
branches.cn: 湖中的生物

branches.en: local biology
branches.cn: 本地生物

intro.en: Biology builds biologist and biological with -ist and -ical.
intro.cn: biology 可加 -ist、-ical 构成 biologist 与 biological。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek bios, life, and logos, word.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语 bios（生命）与 logos（言说）。

definition_zh: 焦躁不安的；无法安睡的；不停活动的
definition_en: unable to stay still or relax because of worry, excitement or boredom
core_image: 一只在笼中来回踱步、怎么也停不下来的动物
scene: 等待面试结果的整夜，他焦躁不安，反复起身走动。 All night while waiting for the interview result, he was restless and kept getting up to walk around.
sceneCN: 这里 restless 是「焦躁不安的」（第 1 个义项：无法放松安静）；句意：等待面试结果的整夜，他焦躁不安，反复起身走动。

pos.zh: 焦躁不安的；无法安睡的；不停活动的

senses.title: Unable to stay calm
senses.definition: unable to relax or stay still because of worry or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 因担忧或兴奋而无法放松或安静下来
senses.example: The children grew restless before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前孩子们变得焦躁不安。
senses.why: Restless literally means without rest, so the mind or body cannot settle.
senses.whyCN: restless 字面意为「没有休息」，所以身心都安定不下来。

senses.title: Without proper sleep
senses.definition: not giving or getting rest, especially sleep
senses.definitionCN: 不能让人休息，尤其是不能安睡
senses.example: She spent a restless night thinking about the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她想着考试，辗转难眠了一整夜。
senses.why: A night without rest is restless because sleep never settles.
senses.whyCN: 没有休息的一夜之所以 restless，是因为睡眠始终没有安稳下来。

senses.title: Always moving
senses.definition: never still, moving about all the time
senses.definitionCN: 从不静止，总是动来动去
senses.example: A restless mind keeps turning over new ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗不停运转的头脑总是翻来覆去地想着新点子。
senses.why: The same lack of rest can describe constant mental or physical motion.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「不得休息」也能形容思绪或身体持续不停的移动。

intro.en: Restless joins the Old English noun rest with the suffix -less, meaning without.
intro.cn: restless 由古英语名词 rest 加后缀 -less（没有）构成。

items.en: Ræst means a period of rest or sleep.
items.cn: ræst 意为休息或睡眠的一段时间。

items.en: The suffix -leas means without.
items.cn: 后缀 -leas 意为没有。

items.en: Restles describes a person who cannot be still.
items.cn: restles 形容无法安静的人。

items.en: Restless extends from sleeplessness to mental unease.
items.cn: restless 从失眠扩展到内心的不安。

items.en: Restless energy names motion that will not settle.
items.cn: restless energy 指无法安定的活动力。

note.en: Restless belongs to the family of rest and is close to words for unease.
note.cn: restless 属于 rest 词族，并与表示不安的词相近。

entries.definition: a period of relaxation
giving a feeling of rest
in an uneasy way
slightly worried or uncomfortable
showing strong nervous excitement
making small restless movements

normalIntro.en: Restless is rest plus less: no rest at all, so the body keeps moving.
normalIntro.cn: restless 就是 rest 加 less：一点休息都没有，所以身体停不下来。

normal.en: A restless night is a night without real sleep.
normal.cn: a restless night 就是没有真正睡好的一夜。

normal.en: Children grow restless when they wait too long.
normal.cn: 孩子等得太久就会变得焦躁。

normal.en: Restless energy is power that will not sit still.
normal.cn: restless energy 是坐不住的精力。

normal.en: The adverb restlessly describes pacing up and down.
normal.cn: 副词 restlessly 描述来回踱步。

normal.en: Compare restful: restful calms you, restless will not let you calm down.
normal.cn: 对比 restful：restful 让你平静，restless 让你平静不下来。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum that never stops swinging.
abstract.cn: 想象一只永不停摆的钟摆。

abstract.en: Imagine a page turning itself over again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸自己不停地翻来翻去。

abstract.en: Think of a chair that cannot hold anyone for long.
abstract.cn: 想象一把谁也坐不久的椅子。

examples.en: He felt restless and could not sit through the meeting.
examples.cn: 他坐立不安，无法把会开完。

examples.en: The baby was restless because of the heat.
examples.cn: 因为天气热，宝宝睡得很不安稳。

examples.en: Her restless fingers tapped the table all afternoon.
examples.cn: 一下午她的手指都不安分地敲着桌子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rest（休息）＋ less（少）」——休息太少，人就焦躁不安；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ræst（休息）＋ -leas（没有）→ restles → restless，核心义「得不到休息、安定不下来」。

sensesIntro.en: Restless starts with an unsettled mind, moves to broken sleep, and ends with constant motion.
sensesIntro.cn: restless 先指内心不安，再指睡眠不稳，最后指持续不停的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a caged animal pacing and never lying down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只在笼中来回踱步、从不躺下的动物。

branches.en: The basic sense is an unsettled, worried state.
branches.cn: 基本义是心神不宁、担忧的状态。

branches.en: Sleep offers no rest, so the night is broken.
branches.cn: 睡眠得不到休息，于是整夜断断续续。

branches.en: The body or mind never stops moving.
branches.cn: 身体或思绪从不停下。

branches.en: Worry at night produces both unease and poor sleep.
branches.cn: 夜里的担忧同时带来不安与失眠。

branches.en: Unease shows itself as pacing and fidgeting.
branches.cn: 不安会表现为踱步和坐立不安。

intro.en: Restless is a native English compound of a noun and a negative suffix.
intro.cn: restless 是由名词和否定后缀构成的英语本族复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the word grew inside Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，是在古英语内部形成的。

items.example: The suffix -ful gives the opposite feeling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 给出相反的感觉。

definition_zh: 加速；加快；使提前
definition_en: to move faster, or to make something happen sooner
core_image: 一辆车驶出弯道，猛踩油门，尾灯拉成一条线
scene: 车队驶出弯道，车手猛踩油门，速度一下子提了上去。 The car accelerated smoothly onto the highway.
sceneCN: 这里的 accelerate 指「加速」（第 1 个义项：使运动速度变快）；句意是汽车平稳加速驶上高速。

senses.title: To move faster
senses.definition: moves or travels at increasing speed
senses.definitionCN: 以越来越快的速度移动或行驶
senses.example: The train accelerated as it left the station.
senses.exampleCN: 列车离站时加快了速度。
senses.why: The Latin root celer means swift, so the first sense is simply a vehicle gaining speed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 celer 意为迅捷，第一个义项就是交通工具把速度提上去。

senses.title: To quicken a process
senses.definition: makes a process happen more quickly
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程发生得更快
senses.example: The new software accelerated the work.
senses.exampleCN: 新软件加快了工作进度。
senses.why: A process can gain speed the way a car does, so the verb moves from the road to daily work.
senses.whyCN: 过程能像车一样提速，动词于是从路面走到了日常工作。

senses.title: To bring forward
senses.definition: moves an event to an earlier time
senses.definitionCN: 把某个事件移到更早的时间
senses.example: They accelerated the launch by a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把发布提前了一个月。
senses.why: Making a date come sooner is speeding up the calendar rather than a body.
senses.whyCN: 让日期早点到来，加速的是日历，而不是物体。

intro.en: The word joins a Latin prefix meaning towards with a root meaning swift.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示「朝向」的拉丁前缀与意为「迅捷」的词根接在一起。

items.en: celer meant swift, as in a fast horse.
items.cn: celer 意为迅捷，如快马一般。

items.en: celeritas named speed itself.
items.cn: celeritas 指速度本身。

items.en: accelerare meant to hasten something.
items.cn: accelerare 意为催促、加快某事。

items.en: accelerate entered English as a verb of hastening.
items.cn: accelerate 进入英语时是表示「催促」的动词。

items.en: it now covers cars, growth, learning and disease.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖车辆、增长、学习与疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acceleration family; the near-meaning group is other verbs of hurrying.
note.cn: 形近组是 acceleration 词族；近义组是别的表示催促的词。

entries.definition: an increase in speed
a pedal or machine that speeds things up
getting faster and faster
tending to speed something up
to make something happen sooner
to become or make faster
to make a process run faster
to move or work faster
to help something advance

normalIntro.en: These hints follow celer, the Latin word for swift.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着拉丁语里表示「迅捷」的 celer。

normal.en: celer is Latin for swift, the heart of the word.
normal.cn: celer 是拉丁语的「迅捷」，正是词的核心。

normal.en: ad- means towards, so accelerate is to move towards speed.
normal.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「朝向」，accelerate 就是朝速度去。

normal.en: -ate makes a verb out of the Latin stem.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁词干变成动词。

normal.en: accelerator is both the pedal and a machine part.
normal.cn: accelerator 既指油门，也指加速装置。

normal.en: growth, change and progress are the usual objects of the verb.
normal.cn: 增长、变革与进步是这个词常见的宾语。

abstract.en: See a speedometer needle swing to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象速度表的指针猛地扫向右边。

abstract.en: Picture a runner bursting off the starting line.
abstract.cn: 想象短跑者冲出起跑线。

abstract.en: Think of calendar pages flipping faster and faster.
abstract.cn: 想象日历的纸页越翻越快。

examples.en: The car accelerated smoothly onto the highway.
examples.cn: 汽车平稳加速驶上高速。

examples.en: New laws may accelerate the pace of change.
examples.cn: 新法律可能加快变革的步伐。

examples.en: Warm weather accelerates the growth of plants.
examples.cn: 温暖的天气加快植物生长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞勒瑞特」——阿克一踩油门，车子嗖地窜了出去。

root: 拉丁语 accelerare（加快），由 ad-（朝向）与 celer（迅捷）构成，本义「使变快」，引申为促进、提前。

sensesIntro.en: One verb of speed covers the car, the work in hand and the date on the calendar.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示速度的动词，管着车子、手上的工作与日历上的日期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pedal pressed down and a needle climbing.
core.cn: 核心意象：踏板踩下，指针攀升。

branches.en: a body gaining speed on the road
branches.cn: 在路面上提速的物体

branches.en: work and growth pushed along faster
branches.cn: 被推得更快的工作与增长

branches.en: a date moved nearer
branches.cn: 被挪近的日期

branches.en: speed shared by machines and by processes
branches.cn: 机器与过程共有的「快」

branches.en: haste that shortens work and time at once
branches.cn: 同时缩短工作与时间的催促

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb made of a prefix, a root and a verb ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由前缀、词根与动词词尾组成，是一枚拉丁语动词。

latinIntro.en: The root celer, swift, also survives in celerity, meaning speed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 celer（迅捷）也留在 celerity（迅速）里。

definition_zh: 激光；激光束；激光器；激光技术
definition_en: a device that produces a narrow, intense beam of light; the beam itself; the technology that uses such beams
core_image: 一束极细的红色光线从仪器里射出，笔直穿过空气
scene: 手术室里，医生用一束极细的光切开组织，边缘几乎看不到血。 The surgeon used a laser to remove the tissue without cutting.
sceneCN: 这里是「激光」（第 1 个义项：高度集中的光束）；句意是外科医生用激光去除组织，而不用刀切。图中可辨识物件：手术灯、仪器面板、红色光束。

pos.zh: 激光；激光束；激光器；激光技术

derivatives.zh: 由 laser 逆构而成的动词，义为「发出激光；用激光处理」
由激光角膜手术的英文首字母缩略而成，义为「激光视力矫正手术」
由 laser 与 guided 复合而成，义为「激光制导的」

senses.title: A narrow, intense beam of light
senses.definition: a narrow, very intense beam of light in which the waves travel together
senses.definitionCN: 波列高度一致、又细又强的光束
senses.example: The laser cut through the metal sheet in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 激光几秒钟就切穿了金属板。
senses.why: The acronym was built to name light amplified into a tight, orderly beam, so the beam itself became the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个缩略词本是为描述被放大成紧密有序光束的光而造，于是光束本身成了日常义项。

senses.title: A device that produces such a beam
senses.definition: a machine or device that produces a laser beam
senses.definitionCN: 产生激光束的机器或装置
senses.example: The lab bought a new laser for the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为这项实验买了一台新的激光器。
senses.why: Because the acronym first named the process and the apparatus, the device sense stayed beside the beam it produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个缩略词最初兼指过程和装置，所以「装置」义一直与它产生的光束并存。

senses.title: The technology or use of such beams
senses.definition: the use of laser beams in medicine, industry, scanning or entertainment
senses.definitionCN: 激光在医疗、工业、扫描或娱乐中的使用
senses.example: Laser is now common in eye surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 激光如今在白内障等眼科手术中很常见。
senses.why: As the device spread into hospitals, workshops and shops, the word came to stand for the whole technology rather than one beam.
senses.whyCN: 随着装置进入医院、车间和商店，这个词逐渐指整套技术，而不只是一束光。

intro.en: Laser is not an inherited word but a twentieth-century acronym, coined from the initials of a scientific phrase and then turned into an ordinary noun.
intro.cn: laser 不是世代相传的词，而是二十世纪由科学短语首字母造出的缩略词，随后变成普通名词。

items.en: Physicists were amplifying microwaves with a device called a maser and wanted the same effect with light.
items.cn: 二十世纪五十年代，物理学家用称为 maser 的装置放大微波，并想在光上实现同样效果。

items.en: Gordon Gould is generally credited with coining the acronym laser from light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation.
items.cn: 一般认为，戈登·古尔德在 1957 年用「受激辐射光放大」的英文首字母造出 laser 这一缩略词。

items.en: Schawlow and Townes published the optical principle that made a light maser practical.
items.cn: 1958 年，肖洛与汤斯发表了使「光激射器」可行的光学原理。

items.en: Theodore Maiman built the first working ruby laser, and the word quickly entered newspapers.
items.cn: 1960 年，梅曼造出第一台可工作的红宝石激光器，这个词随即进入报端。

items.en: Modern English uses laser for the beam, the device and the technology, and has derived the verb lase.
items.cn: 现代英语用 laser 指光束、装置和技术，并由此派生出动词 lase。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the acronym's relatives and its predecessor; the near-meaning group collects words for light and beams.
note.cn: 形近组收这个缩略词的派生形式与前身；近义组收表示光和光束的词。

entries.definition: The microwave predecessor of the laser, using the same amplification principle.
entries.definitionCN: 激光器的微波前身，使用同样的放大原理。

entries.definition: To emit laser light or to treat something with a laser.
entries.definitionCN: 发出激光，或用激光处理某物。

entries.definition: A form of eye surgery that reshapes the cornea with a laser.
entries.definitionCN: 用激光重塑角膜的一种眼科手术。

entries.definition: A directed line of light or other radiation.
entries.definitionCN: 定向射出的一束光或其他辐射。

entries.definition: A single line or narrow stream of light.
entries.definitionCN: 一条光线或一束很细的光。

entries.definition: Energy travelling through space, including light and heat.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间中传播的能量，包括光和热。

normalIntro.en: The word is an acronym, so its memory hooks are the scientific phrase behind it and the family of devices and uses built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是缩略词，所以记忆抓手是它背后的科学短语，以及由它构成的装置与用途词族。

normal.en: Laser stands for light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation, which is a description rather than a root.
normal.cn: laser 代表「受激辐射光放大」，这是一句描述，而不是一个词根。

normal.en: The term was coined in 1957, which makes laser far younger than most words in this book.
normal.cn: 这个词造于 1957 年，因此比本书中大多数词年轻得多。

normal.en: Maser is the microwave older sibling; replace the m with l and the same idea becomes light.
normal.cn: maser 是它在微波波段的前身；把 m 换成 l，同一个想法就变成了光。

normal.en: Lase is a back-formation from laser, created by speakers who needed a verb for producing the beam.
normal.cn: lase 是从 laser 逆构出的动词，由需要表达「发出光束」的人造出来。

normal.en: Laser beam, laser printer and laser surgery are compounds that show the device spreading into new fields.
normal.cn: laser beam、laser printer 和 laser surgery 这些复合词显示装置正扩散到新的领域。

abstract.en: A word made from initials reminds us that language keeps building new roots out of new science.
abstract.cn: 由首字母造出的词提醒人：语言一直在用新科学搭建新的词根。

abstract.en: Light that is forced into one orderly direction becomes a tool, which is why the beam and the device share a name.
abstract.cn: 被约束到同一方向的光成了工具，所以光束与装置共用同一个名字。

abstract.en: Laser shows a technology so vivid that its acronym stops sounding like an acronym and starts feeling like a word.
abstract.cn: laser 说明一种技术足够鲜明，以至于它的缩略词不再像缩略词，而开始像一个普通单词。

examples.en: The laser cut through the metal sheet in seconds.
examples.cn: 激光几秒钟就切穿了金属板。

examples.en: The lab bought a new laser for the experiment.
examples.cn: 实验室为这项实验买了一台新的激光器。

examples.en: Laser is now common in eye surgery.
examples.cn: 激光如今在眼科手术中很常见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「镭射」——这是 laser 的音译说法，指激光；记住 laser 就是激光。

root: 二十世纪缩略词，由「受激辐射光放大」这一科学短语的英文首字母组成，没有拉丁语或日耳曼语词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is coherent light; the senses divide into the beam, the machine that makes it, and the technology built around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是高度一致的光；义项由此分为光束、制造光束的机器，以及围绕它形成的技术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin red line of light leaving a machine and crossing the air without spreading.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束细红线从机器射出，穿过空气而不散开。

branches.en: a thin red line crossing a dark room
branches.cn: 暗室里划过的一道细红线

branches.en: a boxy machine humming on a lab bench
branches.cn: 实验台上嗡嗡作响的方形机器

branches.en: a surgeon's hand guided by a pencil of light
branches.cn: 一束笔直的光引导着外科医生的手

branches.en: a factory floor where metal is cut without a blade
branches.cn: 不用刀片就能切开金属的车间

branches.en: a cat chasing a moving dot from a laser pointer
branches.cn: 猫追着激光笔投下的移动小点

intro.en: The word is an acronym whose parts are ordinary English scientific terms; its later compounds and suffixes grow from the whole acronym.
intro.cn: 这个词是缩略词，其组成是普通的英语科学术语；后来的复合词与后缀则从整个缩略词上生长出来。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

the microwave predecessor of the laser
items.meaningCN: 微波激射器；激光器的前身

items.meaning: a beam produced by a laser

definition_zh: 铜；铜币；警察（英式口语）；铜色的
definition_en: a reddish brown metal, a coin made of it, or a British slang word for a police officer
core_image: 一截裸露的铜线在灯下泛出暖红的光
scene: 电工剥开电线外皮，露出一段发亮的金属。 The wire is made of copper, so it bends easily.
sceneCN: 这里 copper 指「铜」（第 1 个义项：一种红棕色的金属）；句意是这根导线是铜做的，所以容易弯。

senses.title: The reddish metal
senses.definition: a soft reddish brown metal used for wires and pipes
senses.definitionCN: 一种柔软的红棕色金属，用于制线和管道
senses.example: Copper carries electricity very well.
senses.exampleCN: 铜的导电性很好。
senses.why: The metal was once dug on Cyprus, and the island gave it its name.
senses.whyCN: 这种金属曾在塞浦路斯开采，岛名就成了它的名字。

senses.title: A low value coin
senses.definition: a coin of small value, once made of copper
senses.definitionCN: 面值很小的硬币，早年用铜铸成
senses.example: He paid with a handful of coppers.
senses.exampleCN: 他付了一把铜币。
senses.why: Small money is named by the metal it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 小面值的钱，用铸它的金属来命名。

senses.title: A police officer in slang
senses.definition: a British slang word for a police officer
senses.definitionCN: 英式俚语中对警察的称呼
senses.example: A copper asked to see his licence.
senses.exampleCN: 一名警察要求看他的执照。
senses.why: The slang may come from the old verb to cop, to catch.
senses.whyCN: 这个俚语可能来自古动词 cop，意为抓住。

intro.en: Copper comes from Latin cuprum, a shortening of Cyprium aes, metal of Cyprus, where the ore was mined.
intro.cn: copper 来自拉丁语 cuprum，是 Cyprium aes（塞浦路斯的金属）的缩写，因为当地开采铜矿。

items.en: Kypros was the Greek name of the island of Cyprus.
items.cn: Kypros 是塞浦路斯岛的希腊语名称。

items.en: Cyprium aes meant the metal that came from Cyprus.
items.cn: Cyprium aes 意为来自塞浦路斯的金属。

items.en: Cuprum shortened the phrase and named the metal alone.
items.cn: cuprum 缩短了这个短语，单独指这种金属。

items.en: English borrowed the word as copor from Latin speakers.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语使用者那里借来了 copor 这个词。

items.en: The spelling settled toward copper, close to the modern form.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 copper，接近今天的形式。

items.en: Slang added the sense of a coin and of a police officer.
items.cn: 俚语又添上了铜币与警察两个含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short -op- shape, and the meaning group names other metals and alloys.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 -op- 外形，近义组列出其他金属与合金。

entries.definition: a police officer in informal speech
a thing made to match another
a playful jump or a pickled bud
an alloy of copper and tin
an alloy of copper and zinc
a hard material that conducts heat and power
entries.definitionCN: 能导热导电的坚硬材料

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a warm red wire, then move to small coins and to a British officer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一根暖红的电线开始，再到小面值硬币，最后到英国警察。

normal.en: Copper the metal, copper the coin, copper the officer: one word, three red-brown things.
normal.cn: 铜、铜币、警察：一个词，三样带红褐色意味的东西。

normal.en: The metal is named after Cyprus, so think of a sunny island.
normal.cn: 这种金属因塞浦路斯得名，可以想成一座阳光岛。

normal.en: Copper wire bends easily, which is why old houses still use it.
normal.cn: 铜线容易弯，所以老房子至今还在用。

normal.en: The slang officer and the metal share one word by accident of history.
normal.cn: 俚语里的警察与这种金属，因历史的巧合共用一个词。

normal.en: Say cop plus per to keep the two p sounds apart.
normal.cn: 读作 cop 加 per，把两个 p 音分开。

abstract.en: Picture a coil of wire glowing under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下一卷发亮的电线。

abstract.en: Picture a palm full of small brown coins.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌里盛满褐色小硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a green roof turning red brown with age.
abstract.cn: 想象铜屋顶随着岁月由绿转成红褐。

examples.en: The old pot is lined with copper.
examples.cn: 这口旧锅内壁衬着铜。

examples.en: He saved every copper in a tin.
examples.cn: 他把每一枚铜币都存进一个铁罐。

examples.en: A copper stood at the end of the lane.
examples.cn: 一名警察站在小巷尽头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 copper 记成 cop 加 per：警察制服上的纽扣常是铜的，铜与警察就共用这个词。

root: 源自拉丁语 cuprum，为 Cyprium aes（塞浦路斯的金属）的缩写，因古代铜矿多采自塞浦路斯岛，后引申出铜币与警察等义。

sensesIntro.en: From a metal named after an island, to the small coin made from it, and to a slang name for an officer.
sensesIntro.cn: 从以岛命名的金属，到用它铸成的小硬币，最后到警察的俚语称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare copper wire shining warm red.
core.cn: 核心意象：一截裸铜线泛着暖红的光。

branches.en: A soft red metal runs through wires and pipes.
branches.cn: 一种柔软的红金属穿行在电线与管道里。

branches.en: The same metal once made the smallest money.
branches.cn: 同一种金属曾铸成最小的钱币。

branches.en: Slang borrows the word for an officer who catches people.
branches.cn: 俚语借这个词来称抓人的警察。

branches.en: Metal and coin are linked by what the coin is made of.
branches.cn: 金属与硬币由铸币材料连在一起。

branches.en: Both extra senses grew in everyday British speech.
branches.cn: 两个引申义都生长于英国日常口语。

intro.en: Copper rests on Latin cuprum, from the island name Cyprus, and takes -y and -plate in English.
intro.cn: copper 源于拉丁语 cuprum，出自岛名塞浦路斯，在英语里又能加 -y 与 -plate。

latinIntro.en: The copper base cupr- also appears in cuprous and cupric, the two chemical forms.
latinIntro.cn: 铜的词基 cupr- 也出现在 cuprous 与 cupric 这两个化学用语中。

items.meaning: a plate of copper used for printing

senses.title: The British spelling

senses.definitionCN: 公制重量单位 gram 的英式拼写
senses.example: The recipe calls for two hundred grammes of flour.
senses.exampleCN: 配方上写着二百克面粉。

senses.title: The older written form
senses.definition: the older written form of the unit still found in old books

definition_zh: 无论什么；不管什么；任何…的事物；（用于否定）一点也不；（口语）无所谓
definition_en: used to say that any thing at all is meant, or that something does not matter, or with a negative as a stronger not at all
core_image: 一只空篮子被举起来，谁往里放什么都照收
scene: 收摊的人把筐一举：「剩下什么都没关系，都放进来。」 Whatever you decide, tell me tonight.
sceneCN: 这里 whatever 是「无论什么」（第 1 个义项：表示任何一种情况都包括）；句意为你无论决定什么，今晚都告诉我。举起的空篮子照收一切，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Any thing at all
senses.definition: used to name no particular thing but to cover every possible one
senses.definitionCN: 不指名某一事物，而把一切可能都包含在内
senses.example: Whatever you decide, tell me tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 你无论决定什么，今晚都告诉我。
senses.why: The ending -ever adds the idea of any to what, so the question word stops asking and starts covering.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ever 为 what 添上「任何」之意，疑问词于是停止提问，转而包揽一切。

senses.title: It does not matter
senses.definition: used to say that the choice or difference does not affect the result
senses.definitionCN: 表示某种选择或差别不影响结果
senses.example: Whatever you say, the plan is already fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 不管你怎么说，计划已经定了。
senses.why: If every case is covered, the differences stop mattering, so the word shrugs in conversation.
senses.whyCN: 若一切情况都被包含，差别也就不再重要，于是这个词在口语里成了耸肩。

senses.title: Not at all, after a negative
senses.definition: used after a negative noun phrase to strengthen it, meaning not any amount
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定名词短语之后加强语气，表示任何一点也没有
senses.example: There was no reason whatever for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误一点理由也没有。
senses.why: Covering every case also means not a single case, and after not the same word becomes the strongest form of none.
senses.whyCN: 包揽一切也意味着一个都不剩，放在 not 之后，这个词就成了最强的「全无」。

senses.title: A shrug in speech
senses.titleCN: （口语，单独用）随便；爱怎样怎样
senses.definition: said alone to end a subject or to show that one does not care
senses.definitionCN: 单独说出来，用来结束话题或表示不在意
senses.example: Whatever. We are not going to agree tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 随便吧。今晚我们是谈不拢的。
senses.why: A single word that closes the question has no need of a sentence, so the shrug became a word of its own.
senses.whyCN: 一个词就能关掉这个问题，不需要整句，于是耸肩自己成了一个独立的词。

intro.en: Whatever is a Middle English compound of what and ever, and the pattern copied who, which and where to build whoever, whichever and wherever.
intro.cn: whatever 是中古英语里 what 与 ever 的复合词，这个模式后来照搬到 who、which、where，造出 whoever、whichever、wherever。

items.en: The elements were separate: hwæt the pronoun and æfre ever, with no compound yet.
items.cn: 两个成分各自独立：代词 hwæt 与 æfre（ever），尚未组成复合词。

items.en: Writers joined what and ever into a single word, and it quickly took over the free relative clause.
items.cn: 作者把 what 与 ever 连成一个词，它很快接管了自由关系从句。

items.en: The same union produced whoever and whichever, and whatsoever became its emphatic double.
items.cn: 同样的结合产生了 whoever 与 whichever，whatsoever 则成为它的强调形式。

items.en: In writing, whatever took the place of many older phrases, including all that and that which ever.
items.cn: 在书面语中，whatever 取代了许多旧说法，包括 all that 与 that which ever。

items.en: Twentieth-century conversation cut the phrase whatever you say down to a single flat whatever, a shrug in one word.
items.cn: 二十世纪的口语把 whatever you say 一路缩成平平的一个 whatever，耸肩成了一个词。

note.en: The first group collects the family that ends in -ever, the second the words for any and for not caring.
note.cn: 第一组收以 -ever 结尾的词族，第二组收表示「任何」与「不在意」的说法。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a lid over every possible thing, spreads to the idea that no difference matters, hardens into not at all after a negative, and ends as a one-word shrug.

senses.title: The office of an ambassador
senses.definition: the official building where an ambassador works and often lives
senses.definitionCN: 大使办公、通常也居住的官方建筑
senses.example: She went to the embassy for a visa.
senses.exampleCN: 她去大使馆办签证。
senses.why: The word first named the office or mission of an ambassador, and the building that houses it took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指大使的职务与使命，后来承载这项职务的建筑也沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: The staff of a diplomatic mission
senses.definition: the group of diplomats and officials working at such a mission
senses.definitionCN: 在大使馆工作的外交官与官员群体
senses.example: The embassy was evacuated during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间大使馆人员被疏散。
senses.why: A building and the people inside it are easily named by one word, so embassy also means the mission as a body of staff.
senses.whyCN: 建筑与里面的人很容易共用一个词，所以 embassy 也指由人员组成的整个使团。

senses.title: A deputation, in older use
senses.definition: a group sent on a mission or with a message, an older sense
senses.definitionCN: 被派去执行使命或传递消息的一行人，是较旧的义项
senses.example: An embassy of elders came to ask for peace.
senses.exampleCN: 一队长者前来求和。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a mission or body sent with a purpose, and the modern diplomatic building is a specialised descendant of that travelling group.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是被派出去执行任务的一行人，现代的外交馆舍正是这个出行使团的专门化后代。

intro.en: Embassy goes back to a word for service or mission, and only later settled on the ambassador's residence.

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie embassy to ambassador, then move from the person to the building and the staff.

branches.en: HOUSE AND PEOPLE: one word for the place and its team.

definition_zh: 过度的；过多的；过分的
definition_en: much more than is reasonable or necessary
core_image: 音量开到极限的音响
scene: 邻居家的音乐声太大，已经超出了合理范围。 The music from next door was excessive and far too loud.
sceneCN: 这里 excessive 是「过度的」（第 1 个义项：远远超过合理程度）；句意：邻居家的音乐声太大，已经超出了合理范围。

senses.title: More than reasonable
senses.definition: much more than is reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 远远超过合理程度
senses.example: The noise was excessive for a quiet street.
senses.exampleCN: 在安静的街道上，这噪音太过分了。
senses.why: The word judges an amount as beyond the line.
senses.whyCN: 这个词判定数量越过了界线。

senses.title: Beyond what is allowed
senses.definition: more than is allowed by rules or law
senses.definitionCN: 超过规则或法律允许的范围
senses.example: The guard used excessive force.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫使用了过度武力。
senses.why: A limit exists, and the act crossed it.
senses.whyCN: 界限存在，而行为越过了它。

senses.title: Too high in amount
senses.definition: unreasonably large in number or price
senses.definitionCN: 数量或价格高得不合理
senses.example: They charged an excessive price.
senses.exampleCN: 他们要价过高。
senses.why: A number past sense becomes excessive.
senses.whyCN: 超出常理的数字就是过高的。

intro.en: Excessive comes from Latin excessus, a going beyond.

items.en: Excedere means to go beyond.
items.cn: excedere 意为越过。

items.en: Excessus is the act of going too far.
items.cn: excessus 是走得过头。

items.en: French excessif means overdone.
items.cn: 法语 excessif 意为过度。

items.en: English excessive judges amounts and acts.
items.cn: 英语 excessive 评判数量与行为。

items.en: It appears in law, health and prices.
items.cn: 它出现在法律、健康与价格领域。

note.en: Excessive is beyond reasonable; extreme is at the far end.
note.cn: excessive 指超出合理，extreme 指处于最远端。

normalIntro.cn: excessive 意为越过了合理之线。

normal.en: Excessive noise disturbs a whole street.

abstract.en: Imagine a plate piled far too high.
abstract.cn: 想象盘子堆得过高。

abstract.en: Think of a price tag with one zero too many.
abstract.cn: 想象价签上多写了一个零。

examples.en: Excessive heat closed the schools.
examples.cn: 酷热使学校停课。

examples.en: The worker was punished for excessive delay.

examples.en: Excessive use of water harms the garden.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「excess（过量）＋ ive」——带着过量性质的，就是过度的。

root: 拉丁语 excessus（越出）＋ -ive → excessive，核心义「具有越界、过量性质的」。

sensesIntro.en: Excessive means far more than is reasonable, allowed, or sensible.
sensesIntro.cn: excessive 意为远远超过合理、允许或适度范围。

branches.en: Beyond reason is the general sense.

branches.en: Reason and law both draw a limit.
branches.cn: 常理与法律都画出界线。

branches.en: Force and price can both be pushed too far.

definition_zh: 频繁反复的；不断的；连续的
definition_en: happening again and again, often over a long period
core_image: 门铃刚停又响，一次接着一次
scene: 隔壁装修声隔几分钟就响一阵，让人没法专心。 The continual noise made it hard to work.
sceneCN: 这里 continual 指「频繁反复的」（第 1 个义项：反复发生、其间有短暂停顿）；句意是不断反复的噪音让人难以工作。

pos.zh: 频繁反复的；不断的；连续的

senses.title: Again and again
senses.definition: repeated many times, with short breaks between the times
senses.definitionCN: 多次重复，各次之间只有短暂停顿
senses.example: His continual questions tired the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他没完没了地提问，让老师很累。
senses.why: A quiet that keeps being broken feels worse than one long noise.
senses.whyCN: 一次次被打断的安静，比一整片噪音更难受。

senses.title: Going on without pause
senses.definition: lasting over a long period and seeming never to stop

senses.example: The continual flow of visitors never slowed.
senses.exampleCN: 来访的人流一直没有慢下来。
senses.why: When nothing interrupts, the line simply keeps going.
senses.whyCN: 没有东西打断时，线就一直往前走。

intro.en: Continual comes from Latin continuus, unbroken, from continere, to hold together, with the adjective ending -al added.
intro.cn: continual 来自拉丁语 continuus（相连不断的），源于 continere（保持在一起），后面加上形容词词尾 -al。

items.en: Continere meant to hold things together without a gap.
items.cn: continere 意为把事物无空隙地保持在一起。

items.en: Continuus described what hangs together in an unbroken line.
items.cn: continuus 形容连成一条不断之线的事物。

items.en: Continuare meant to make something go on without stopping.
items.cn: continuare 意为使某事不停地进行下去。

items.en: English continual named what keeps coming back.

items.en: It now often hints at weariness with the repetition.
items.cn: 如今它常暗示对反复的厌烦。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the close continuous family, and the meaning group names other words for what keeps happening.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一词族里容易混用的几个词，近义组列出其他表示反复发生的词。

definition_zh: 使最小化；把……降到最低；贬低；淡化
definition_en: to reduce something to the smallest possible amount or degree, or to treat it as less important than it really is
core_image: 把一只旋钮一路拧到最左端、直到归零的位置
scene: 外科医生先花一小时规划更小的切口，尽量少出血。 The surgeon spent the first hour planning a smaller incision to minimize blood loss.
sceneCN: 这里 minimize 是「把失血降到最低」（第 4 个义项：把损害、伤害减轻到最小）；句意：外科医生用第一个小时设计更小的切口，以把失血降到最低。场景要点：手术灯下的切口标记、旁边摆着的一袋备用血、医生反复比量的尺子；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.zh: 把出错的可能性降到最低
