senses.title: Reach the mathematical minimum
senses.definition: to find or reach the lowest value of a function, quantity, or variable
senses.definitionCN: 求取或达到函数、数量、变量的最低值
senses.example: We minimize the cost function by adjusting both weights at once.
senses.exampleCN: 我们同时调整两个权重，使代价函数取最小值。
senses.why: Latin minimus names the bottom point of a scale. The verb makes an object arrive at that point, so the mathematical sense is the image in its plainest form.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minimus 指刻度的底端。这个动词让对象抵达那个点，因此数学义是这幅意象最朴素的形态。

senses.title: Cost: squeeze the spending down
senses.definition: to keep costs, spending, or prices as low as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把成本、开支或价格保持在尽可能低的水平
senses.example: The airline minimized costs by flying older planes.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司靠飞更旧的飞机把成本压到最低。
senses.why: Cost is a quantity on a dial. Turning that dial to the left end is the budget version of the gesture, and it is the most common business use.
senses.whyCN: 成本是刻度盘上的一个量。把旋钮拧到最左端，就是同一个动作在预算里的版本，也是商业中最常见的用法。

senses.title: Risk: keep the danger small
senses.definition: to reduce the probability or size of a possible harm
senses.definitionCN: 降低某种可能伤害的发生概率或规模
senses.example: Investors diversify their holdings to minimize risk.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者分散持仓，以把风险降到最低。
senses.why: Risk is a probability of loss. Minimizing it moves that probability toward zero, the floor of its own small scale.
senses.whyCN: 风险是损失发生的概率。最小化就是把这个概率推向零，也就是它自己那一小段刻度的底端。

senses.title: Damage: leave as little harm as possible
senses.definition: to limit the harm done to people, property, or the environment
senses.definitionCN: 限制对人、财产或环境造成的伤害
senses.example: The spill was contained to minimize damage to the river.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏被控制住，以把对河流的损害减到最小。
senses.why: Damage is what remains after an accident. Minimizing it means shrinking the remainder, not preventing the accident itself.
senses.whyCN: 损害是事故之后留下的东西。最小化是把这个剩余量缩小，而不是阻止事故本身。

senses.title: Error and delay: shrink the unwanted amount
senses.titleCN: 错误与延误：把不需要的量缩小
senses.definition: to make errors, delays, or other unwanted quantities as small as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把错误、延误或其他不想要的量做到尽可能小
senses.example: Every figure was checked twice to minimize the chance of error.
senses.exampleCN: 每个数字都核对了两遍，以把出错的可能性降到最低。
senses.why: An error is an unwanted quantity on a scale that one would rather see at zero. The same verb now measures what should not be there.
senses.whyCN: 错误是一把尺子上不希望出现的量，人们宁愿它停在零。这个动词于是用来衡量“本不该存在的东西”。

senses.title: Computing: shrink a window to a corner
senses.titleCN: 计算机：把窗口缩到角落
senses.definition: to reduce a window on a screen to a small bar or icon
senses.definitionCN: 把屏幕上的窗口缩成一条小栏或一个图标
senses.example: Click the minus sign to minimize the window.
senses.exampleCN: 点击减号即可把窗口最小化。
senses.why: A window has a size scale whose floor is the smallest allowed bar. The command drives it to that floor, making the metaphor visible as a button.
senses.whyCN: 窗口有一个尺寸刻度，它的底端就是允许的最小条栏。这个命令把窗口推到那层底端，让比喻变成了一个可见的按钮。

senses.title: Downplay a person's role
senses.definition: to make someone's contribution or importance seem smaller than it is
senses.definitionCN: 使某人的贡献或重要性显得比实际更小
senses.example: The report minimizes the role of local volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告贬低了当地志愿者的作用。
senses.why: The scale has moved from things to reputation: a person's role is described as if it occupied a smaller notch than it really does.
senses.whyCN: 尺子从实物移到了名声：一个人的作用被说成只占一个比实际更小的刻度。

senses.title: Soften the seriousness of something
senses.definition: to speak of a problem or danger as less serious than it is
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或危险说得没有实际那么严重
senses.example: Officials minimized the seriousness of the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 官员们淡化了这次泄漏的严重性。
senses.why: Here the quantity being reduced is not the harm but the reported size of the harm; the words shrink the picture while the thing stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 这里被缩小的不是伤害本身，而是伤害被报告出来的大小；话把画面缩小了，而事情本身没有变。

senses.title: Engineering: cut a design down to essentials
senses.titleCN: 工程：把设计削减到本质
senses.definition: to reduce the number of parts, steps, or features in a design to the smallest workable set
senses.definitionCN: 把设计中的零件、步骤或功能削减到可工作的最小集合
senses.example: The redesign minimizes moving parts and therefore wear.
senses.exampleCN: 重新设计把活动部件减到最少，因此也减少了磨损。
senses.why: Fewer parts means less on the scale. Minimizing here is not about one number but about removing everything that is not needed.
senses.whyCN: 零件更少，意味着刻度上的东西更少。这里的最小化不是压一个数字，而是删掉一切不必要的东西。

intro.en: Minimize is an English coinage of 1802 from minimum + -ize. Its Latin base and the later 'belittle' sense are both documented; dates are those given by standard etymological references.
intro.cn: minimize 是 1802 年由 minimum 加 -ize 构成的英语自造词。它的拉丁词基以及后来“贬低”的义项都有记载；年代采用通行词源资料的说法。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'to reduce to a minimum, make as little as possible'. It is an English formation from minimum + -ize, first attested in Bentham.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 1802 年，意为“减到最低、使尽可能小”。它是由 minimum 加 -ize 构成的英语自造词，最早可考的使用者是边沁。

items.en: Minimum entered English meaning 'the smallest portion into which matter is divisible', a sense now obsolete; it came from Latin minimum, the neuter of minimus 'smallest'.
items.cn: minimum 于 17 世纪 60 年代进入英语，意为“物质可分割的最小部分”，这一义项今已废弃；它来自拉丁语 minimum，即 minimus“最小的”的中性形式。

items.en: Latin minimus is the superlative of minor 'smaller', and minor belongs to the same family as minus and minuere 'to lessen'. The whole set describes one end of a scale.
items.cn: 拉丁语 minimus 是 minor“更小的”的最高级，而 minor 与 minus、minuere“减少”同属一个词族。整组词描述的是同一把尺子的一端。

items.en: The family goes back to PIE *mei- (2) 'small', the root also behind diminish, minute, minuscule, minister and minutia.
items.cn: 这个词族可追溯到原始印欧语 *mei-（第二支）“小”，该词根也是 diminish、minute、minuscule、minister、minutia 的来源。

items.en: The sense 'to depreciate, treat slightingly' is recorded. This is the branch that lets minimize mean 'belittle' as well as 'reduce', and it explains why the word can sound evasive.
items.cn: “贬低、轻视地对待”这一义项于 1875 年有记录。正是这一支让 minimize 既能表示“减少”，也能表示“贬低”，也解释了它为何有时听起来像在回避。

items.en: British spelling is minimise. Minimization, minimizer, minimal and minimalism fill out the family. Maximize and minimize are a matched pair, both recorded in 1802 and both used by Bentham.
items.cn: 英式拼写为 minimise。minimization、minimizer、minimal、minimalism 补足了词族。maximize 与 minimize 是一对配套词，都记录于 1802 年，都出自边沁。

note.en: The first group separates the noun, the adjective, the British spelling and the rare short noun. The second group compares minimize with plain reduce, with lessen, with rhetorical downplay, and with its exact opposite, maximize.
note.cn: 第一组区分名词、形容词、英式拼写和一个罕见的短名词；第二组把 minimize 与普通的 reduce、与 lessen、与修辞上的 downplay，以及它的正对面 maximize 作比较。

entries.definition: the smallest amount or degree possible. It is the noun that minimize was built from, not a synonym of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最小数量或程度。它是构成 minimize 的名词词基，而不是这个动词的同义词。

entries.definition: very small in amount or degree. It describes a state, while minimize names the act of bringing that state about.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或程度极小的。它描述一种状态，而 minimize 命名把这种状态造成出来的动作。

entries.definition: the British spelling of minimize, with -ise instead of -ize. It is the same word, not a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: minimize 的英式拼写，用 -ise 代替 -ize。它是同一个词，不是另一个词义。

entries.definition: a tiny amount, or a note of very short duration. It shares the 'small' root but is not a form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的量，或时值很短的音符。它共享“小”的词根，却不是这个动词的词形。

entries.definition: to make something smaller in size or amount. It names the movement, not the floor: a reduced price need not be the lowest possible price.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物在尺寸或数量上变小。它命名移动，而不命名底端：降价并不等于降到可能的最低价格。

entries.definition: to make something smaller in degree or intensity, often a feeling or an effect. It is more literary and more limited than minimize.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事物在程度或强度上变小，常指感受或效果。它比 minimize 更书面，适用范围也更窄。

entries.definition: to make something seem less important than it is. It targets the description, while minimize can target either the thing or the description.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事物显得没有实际那么重要。它针对的是描述，而 minimize 既可针对事物，也可针对描述。

entries.definition: to make as great as possible. It is the exact opposite pole: one verb turns the dial to the left, the other to the right.
entries.definitionCN: 使尽可能大。它正是对立的那一端：一个动词把旋钮向左拧，另一个向右拧。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: minimum + -ize, the Latin superlative minimus, the *mei- 'small' family, and the matched pair minimize / maximize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：minimum 加 -ize、拉丁最高级 minimus、*mei-“小”词族，以及成对的 minimize／maximize。

normal.en: Minimum is the floor of a scale and -ize means 'to make'. Minimize is simply 'to make minimum'.
normal.cn: minimum 是刻度的底端，-ize 意为“使……”。minimize 就是“使达到最小”。

normal.en: Minimus is the Latin superlative of minor 'smaller'; the same root gives minimum, minor, minus and diminish.
normal.cn: minimus 是拉丁语 minor“更小的”的最高级；同一词根还给出 minimum、minor、minus、diminish。

normal.en: Minimize and maximize were both recorded in 1802, both in Bentham: one drives to the floor of the scale, the other to the ceiling.
normal.cn: minimize 与 maximize 都记录于 1802 年，都出自边沁：一个把刻度推到低端，一个推到顶端。

normal.en: In business writing minimize collocates with risk, cost, damage, loss and disruption — unwanted quantities that one wants near zero.
normal.cn: 在商业写作里，minimize 常与 risk、cost、damage、loss、disruption 搭配——都是人们希望接近零的不想要的量。

normal.en: In computing, minimize is the button that shrinks a window to a bar; the smallest allowed bar is the floor of that scale.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，minimize 是把窗口缩成一条栏的按钮；允许的最小条栏就是那把尺子的底端。

abstract.en: Picture a dial with a hard stop at the left end. You can turn it down to the stop and no further; that stop is what minimum means.
abstract.cn: 想象一只左端有硬止点的旋钮。你能把它拧到止点，再也不能多拧一格；那个止点就是 minimum 的含义。

abstract.en: A minimum is a floor, not a direction: minimizing tells you where to stop, not how much effort it takes to get there.
abstract.cn: 最小值是地板，不是方向：minimize 告诉你该停在哪里，却没说你得花多大力气走到那里。

abstract.en: The same verb can shrink a thing or shrink its description. Shrinking the description is what makes minimize sound like an excuse.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既能缩小事物，也能缩小对事物的描述。缩小描述，正是 minimize 听起来像借口的缘故。

examples.en: Keep the lid on the pan to minimize evaporation.
examples.cn: 盖上锅盖，把蒸发减到最少。

examples.en: The company moved its servers abroad to minimize tax.
examples.cn: 这家公司把服务器迁到国外，以把税负压到最低。

examples.en: She minimized her own part in the rescue.
examples.cn: 她把自己在救援中的作用说得很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: “迷你麦子”——把麦子磨得越来越小，最后只剩手心里一小撮 → minimize 最小化、降到最低

root: 由 minimum“最小量”加 -ize“使……”构成，minimum 又来自拉丁语 minimus“最小的”，核心是“把某物拧到刻度的最左端”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of minimize, all from one gesture: a dial is turned to the far left until it reaches the floor, whether the scale measures a function, a cost, a risk, a window, or a person's reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: minimize 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把旋钮一路拧到最左端，直到触底——无论这把尺子量的是函数、成本、风险、窗口，还是一个人的名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial turned to the far left until it stops at the bottom of its scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旋钮被拧到最左端，停在刻度的底端。

branches.en: NUMBERS: a function has a lowest value, and minimizing moves the result down to that value.
branches.cn: 数值：函数有一个最低值，最小化就是把结果压到那个值上。

branches.en: COST AND ENGINEERING: money, risk and moving parts are quantities to be cut down to the floor.
branches.cn: 成本与工程：金钱、风险与活动部件都是要被削到底端的量。

branches.en: HARM: damage and the chance of error are remainders to be shrunk so that as little as possible is left.
branches.cn: 伤害：损害与出错概率都是要被缩小的剩余量，好让最后剩下的尽可能少。

branches.en: INTERFACE: the window shrinks to the smallest allowed bar, its own floor.
branches.cn: 界面：窗口缩到允许的最小条栏，也就是它自己的底端。

branches.en: RHETORIC: a person's role or a danger is made to look smaller than it is, so the scale now measures appearance.
branches.cn: 修辞：一个人的作用或一桩危险被说得比实际小，于是这把尺子量的是“看起来的大小”。

intro.en: Minimize is a complete noun plus a living suffix: minimum + -ize. The same Latin superlative supplies a large family of words about smallness and reduction.
intro.cn: minimize 是一个完整名词加一个活后缀：minimum 加 -ize。同一个拉丁最高级还供应了一大群关于“小”与“减少”的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin minimus 'smallest' is the superlative of minor 'smaller', itself formed from the *mei- family. Minimum is the neuter form used as a noun; minus is a related neuter form meaning 'less'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minimus“最小的”是 minor“更小的”的最高级，而 minor 本身出自 *mei- 词族。minimum 是作名词用的中性形式；minus 是表示“更少”的相关中性形式。

items.meaning: to make as small as possible
items.meaningCN: 使尽可能小；最小化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The plan minimizes the number of transfers.
items.exampleCN: 这个方案把换乘次数减到最少。

items.meaningCN: 最小量；最低限度（-um 为中性最高级词尾）
items.example: The machine needs a minimum of two litres of oil.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器至少需要两升油。

items.meaningCN: 极小的；最低限度的（-al 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 这场风暴造成的损害极小。

items.meaning: the process of reducing something to the least possible
items.meaningCN: 最小化；最小化过程（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Waste minimization saved the plant a fortune.
items.exampleCN: 把浪费最小化为工厂省下一大笔钱。

items.meaning: one who seeks the minimum, or a device that reduces something
items.meaningCN: 求最小值者；把事物压到最小的人或装置（-er 表示行为者）
items.example: As a minimizer, he packs only what fits in one bag.
items.exampleCN: 作为一个凡事求最少的人，他只带一个包能装下的东西。

items.example: The guide advises households to minimise water use.
items.exampleCN: 这份指南建议家庭把用水减到最少。

items.meaning: a tiny amount; a note of short duration
items.meaningCN: 极小的量；短音符（来自拉丁语 minimus）
items.example: The recipe calls for a minim of salt.
items.exampleCN: 这份食谱只要一丁点儿盐。

items.meaningCN: 减去；负号；不利因素（拉丁语 minus，minor 的中性形式）
减少；削弱（di- 离开 + minuere 减少）
items.example: The noise diminished as the train moved away.
items.exampleCN: 火车开远后，噪声渐渐变小。

items.meaningCN: 极小的（作形容词，来自拉丁语 minutus“小的”）
items.example: A minute crack appeared in the glass.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃上出现了一道极细的裂缝。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 更小的；较少的；较年幼的

latinEntries.structure: neuter of minimus, used as a noun
latinEntries.meaningCN: 最小者；最小量（minimus 的中性形式作名词）

definition_zh: 管弦乐队；乐池；正厅前排座位；歌队场地
definition_en: a large group of musicians playing together on strings, woodwind, brass and percussion, and also the space in a theatre where they sit or the seats nearest that space
core_image: 乐池的暗处，一排琴弓同时抬起，等舞台上第一束光落下
scene: 开演前的剧场里，观众还在找座位，乐池的灯先亮了起来，提琴手们把弓一根根试过。 The orchestra tuned slowly while the audience settled in.
sceneCN: 这里是「管弦乐队」（第 1 个义项：在乐池里一起演奏的乐手团体）；句意为观众陆续坐定时，乐队慢慢把音调准。图中可辨识物件：乐池灯、琴弓、乐谱架。

pos.zh: 管弦乐队；乐池；正厅前排座位；歌队场地

derivatives.zh: 由 orchestra 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「管弦乐队的；管弦乐的」
由 orchestra 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「把……编配成管弦乐；精心安排」
由 orchestrate 加名词后缀 -tion 构成，义为「配器；精心编排」

senses.title: A large group of musicians playing together
senses.definition: a large group of musicians, with strings and usually woodwind, brass and percussion, who perform music as one body
senses.definitionCN: 由弦乐等多组乐手组成、作为一个整体演奏的大型乐队
senses.example: The orchestra rehearsed the new symphony twice.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队把这部新交响曲排练了两遍。
senses.why: Greek orchestra named the place where the chorus danced; by the seventeenth century the musicians working in that place took the name, and the group outlived the room.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 orchestra 本指歌队起舞的场地；到十七世纪，在那个场地里奏乐的人反过来用这个词称呼自己，最后留在语言里的是团体，而不是那间屋子。

senses.title: The space where the players sit
senses.definition: the area in front of and usually below the stage where the musicians sit during a performance
senses.definitionCN: 舞台上及其前方、通常低下去的一块区域，演出时乐手坐在那里
senses.example: The violins were already in the orchestra when the curtain rose.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布升起时，小提琴手已经在乐池里就位。
senses.why: The word started life as the name of a space, and English kept that sense for the part of a theatre reserved for players, now often carried by the fuller phrase orchestra pit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就是一块场地的名字，英语一直保留「剧场里留给乐手的那块地方」这层含义，如今多由更完整的 orchestra pit 承担。

senses.title: The front seats on the main floor
senses.definition: the seats on the main floor of a theatre, especially the front part, as opposed to the balcony
senses.definitionCN: 剧场底层、尤其靠前区域的座位，与楼座相对
senses.example: We booked two seats in the orchestra for the opening night.
senses.exampleCN: 首演之夜我们订了两个正厅前排座位。
senses.why: In American theatres the floor area nearest the stage kept the old name of the space, so a ticket can be in the orchestra with no musician involved.
senses.whyCN: 在美国的剧场里，最靠近舞台的底层区域沿用了这块场地的旧名，于是一张票可以写作「in the orchestra」，而整句话和乐手毫无关系。

senses.title: The dancing floor of a Greek theatre
senses.definition: the circular area in front of the stage in an ancient Greek theatre, where the chorus sang and danced
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊剧场中舞台前供歌队歌唱、起舞的圆形场地
senses.example: Archaeologists traced the stone edge of the orchestra at the old theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 考古人员在老剧场里辨认出了歌队场地的石砌边缘。
senses.why: The original Greek word named exactly this dancing floor, so the oldest recorded sense of the English word is a piece of architecture rather than a group of people.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词指的正是这块起舞的场地，所以英语这个词最早记下的含义是一处建筑空间，而不是一群人。

intro.en: Orchestra is a Greek word for a dancing floor that reached English through Latin and the Renaissance study of ancient theatre.
intro.cn: orchestra 是希腊语中表示「起舞场地」的词，经拉丁语与文艺复兴时期对古剧场的研读进入英语。

items.en: The Greek verb orkheisthai meant to dance, and the noun orchestra named the place where the chorus danced in front of the stage.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 orkheisthai 意为跳舞，名词 orchestra 指舞台前歌队起舞的地方。

items.en: In the theatre of Athens the orchestra was the circular floor between the audience and the stage, entered and used by the chorus.
items.cn: 在雅典的剧场中，orchestra 是观众与舞台之间那块圆形地面，歌队由此进出并使用。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word for the same part of a Roman theatre, where the seats nearest the stage were later reserved for senators.
items.cn: 拉丁语借来这个希腊词，指罗马剧场中的同一区域，靠近舞台的座位后来留给元老。

items.en: English writers took the word from Latin for the space before the stage, and then transferred it to the musicians who played in that space.
items.cn: 十七世纪的英语作者从拉丁语借来这个词，先指舞台前的空间，随后把它转给在那里奏乐的乐手。

items.en: Modern English made the group of players the main sense and kept the older spatial senses in orchestra pit and orchestra seats.
items.cn: 现代英语把「演奏团体」定为主要含义，同时把较老的空间含义留在 orchestra pit 与 orchestra seats 里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the orchestral family built on the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group collects other names for groups that make music.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊词干长出的乐队词族；近义组收其他表示「一起奏乐的团体」的说法。

entries.definition: Relating to an orchestra or to music written for one.
entries.definitionCN: 与管弦乐队有关的，或为乐队写的。

entries.definition: To arrange a piece of music for an orchestra, or to plan something carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 为管弦乐队配器，或精心安排一件事。

entries.definition: The art of writing music for an orchestra, or a carefully arranged plan.
entries.definitionCN: 为管弦乐队写作的技艺，或精心编排的方案。

entries.definition: A group of musicians or performers who work as one unit.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一个整体演出的乐手或演员团体。

entries.definition: A large work for orchestra, or an orchestra that plays such works.
entries.definitionCN: 为管弦乐队写的大型作品，或演奏这类作品的乐团。

entries.definition: A smaller group of players, often with drums and brass.
entries.definitionCN: 人数较少、常含鼓与铜管的乐队。

normalIntro.en: Every form in this entry grows from a Greek word for a dancing floor, so the mnemonics move between the room and the people who fill it.
normalIntro.cn: 这一条里所有形式都长自希腊语中「起舞场地」这个词，联想便在房间和填满它的人之间来回。

normal.en: Orchestra began as a Greek word for a dancing floor, so the oldest picture in it is feet moving on stone.
normal.cn: orchestra 最初是希腊语里「起舞场地」的说法，所以它最老的画面是石地上走动的脚步。

normal.en: The name then moved from the floor to the players standing on it.
normal.cn: 这个名字随后从场地挪到站在场地上的乐手身上。

normal.en: Orchestra pit keeps the old room sense, while orchestra alone now usually means the group.
normal.cn: orchestra pit 保留了「房间」旧义，而单独用的 orchestra 现在通常指团体。

normal.en: Orchestral adds -al and turns the players into an adjective.
normal.cn: orchestral 加 -al，把乐手团体变成形容词。

normal.en: Orchestrate adds -ate and turns arranging for that group into a verb.
normal.cn: orchestrate 加 -ate，把为这个团体配器变成动词。

abstract.en: A hall dark except for the pit, where many pairs of hands move as one.
abstract.cn: 大厅全暗，只有乐池亮着，许多双手在那里合成一个动作。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a floor now means the people who make the floor noisy.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经指地板的词，现在指把地板弄得热闹起来的那群人。

abstract.en: The room is small, but what it sends into the hall is larger than the room.
abstract.cn: 那间屋子很小，可它送进大厅的声音比屋子大得多。

examples.en: The orchestra rehearsed the new symphony twice.
examples.cn: 乐队把这部新交响曲排练了两遍。

examples.en: The violins were already in the orchestra when the curtain rose.
examples.cn: 幕布升起时，小提琴手已经在乐池里就位。

examples.en: We booked two seats in the orchestra for the opening night.
examples.cn: 首演之夜我们订了两个正厅前排座位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥凯斯特拉」——一群人挤在台下那块小地方，节拍一起走；记住 orchestra 是管弦乐队。

root: 希腊语 ὀρχήστρα（歌队起舞的场地）源自 ὀρχεῖσθαι（跳舞），经拉丁语 orchestra 进入英语；词义从场地转到在场地上奏乐的团体。拉丁语 orchestra 本身也只是借自希腊语，并非独立的同族词，因此不列拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place where people make music together; the senses run from that room to the players, to the seats, and back to the ancient dancing floor.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「人们一起奏乐的那块地方」；义项从这块地方走到人，再到座位，最后回到古代那块起舞的场地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of bows lifted together in the dark of a pit.
core.cn: 核心意象：乐池的暗处，一排琴弓同时抬起。

branches.en: a conductor raising both hands before the first beat
branches.cn: 指挥在第一个拍子前抬起双手

branches.en: lamps coming on over empty music stands below the stage
branches.cn: 舞台下方空谱架上的灯亮起

branches.en: a ticket printed with a row and a seat number
branches.cn: 一张印着排号与座号的票

branches.en: chorus members circling a stone floor
branches.cn: 歌队绕着石砌地面走成圆圈

branches.en: a guide pointing to the worn edge of an ancient stage
branches.cn: 向导指着古剧场舞台磨损的边缘

intro.en: Orchestra is not built from English pieces but from a Greek noun and its verb, with later English suffixes making the adjective and the verb of arranging.
intro.cn: orchestra 不是用英语部件拼成的，而是来自一个希腊名词及其动词，后来再加英语后缀造出形容词与「配器」动词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin, and Latin orchestra is itself a borrowing from Greek rather than a native cognate, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自希腊语，拉丁语 orchestra 本身也是从希腊语借去的，并非本土同族词，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.meaning: the dancing place of the chorus
place or instrument of an action
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：动作的场所或工具

items.meaning: the same space in a Roman theatre
items.meaningCN: 罗马剧场中的同一区域

items.meaning: a group of musicians, or the space they use
to arrange music for an orchestra, or to plan something
items.meaningCN: 为管弦乐队配器；精心安排
items.exampleCN: 她精心策划了整个活动。
